jobs.description:
Director, AP Japanese Language and Culture, Curriculum and Assessment

College Board – AP & I

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type:This is a full-time position


About the Team

The AP Curriculum and Assessment Team at College Board (125+ staff) collaborates with colleagues across all aspects of the AP Program to develop, manage, and deliver AP’s 43 courses in a wide variety of subject areas. AP® is a rigorous academic program built on the commitment, passion, and hard work of students and educators from secondary schools and higher education. AP provides willing and academically prepared high school students with the opportunity to study and learn at the college level. AP’s course teams comprised of educators and disciplinary experts ensure that course curricula are aligned to higher education expectations and reflect the state of the art in the discipline, contribute to instructional resources and tools for teachers, and develop assessments that allow students in these courses to demonstrate their mastery of course content and skills. AP leads in strategic use of AI to expand student access, strengthen instructional design and professional support, and enhance assessment creation and exam analysis. The English, World Languages, and Arts department, which includes English Literature, English Language, Spanish Language, Japanese Language, French Language, German Language, Japanese Language, Japanese Language, Latin, Music Theory, Spanish Literature, and Art and Design is currently comprised of approximately 35 people supporting 14 courses in the AP portfolio. 


About the Opportunity

As the Director I, AP Japanese Language and Culture you will be responsible for preserving and improving the quality and validity of the AP Program’s core deliverables within the subject domain: the exam, the course curriculum, and the professional development content. You are also responsible for item development and management from authoring to administration; training and collaborating with subject-matter experts (SMEs), typically college professors and secondary school teachers. You will ethically and effectively integrate AI technologies in assessment creation and review. This includes judiciously using AI assisted tools to support fairness, validity, and innovation in AP assessments. You will train SMEs on assessment development protocols, translate between academics and technical experts (psychometricians), and collaborate to develop formative assessment materials and resources to support AP Japanese Language and Culture teachers worldwide. You will serve as a point of contact in AP for committees and communities of subject-matter experts and will be responsible for the curriculum and assessment for AP Japanese Language and Culture, and, in partnership with other AP teams, further the strategic growth of AP Japanese Language and Culture across the globe. Additionally, you may have the opportunity to present, speak, and moderate dialogue with academic and membership audiences to ensure that ongoing change and improvement within AP courses and exams is understood, accepted, and supported in secondary and post-secondary educational communities.  


In this role, you will:


Assessment Development and Scoring (45-75%)  

  • Serve as an assessment leader for AP Japanese Language and Culture, with primary responsibility for assessment development for AP Japanese Language and Culture. Your work in developing and revising test content is of the quality that requires only minimal adjustments based on feedback from your manager and other program leaders. 
  • Independently lead processes for authoring and revising assessment content, including training educator constituents and leveraging generative AI to author and/or review assessment content, improving and/or making more efficient assessment processes and outputs.
  • Independently lead the development and management of assessment content (formative and summative) and scoring materials for AP Japanese Language and Culture through iterative review stages with multiple internal and external stakeholders, including the AP Japanese Language and Culture Team, Assessment Production team, Test Development Committee, and the Chief Reader, as appropriate.
  • Independently lead the development of assessment forms for AP Japanese Language and Culture, ensuring the AP Exam development aligns with approved curricula and test specifications.
  • Lead multiple face-to-face, weekend meetings, and virtual meetings (during work week, evenings, or weekends) annually with the AP Japanese Language and Culture Test Development Committee. You strategize and develop an agenda and approach to ensure the committee’s meeting time is of the highest productivity; you successfully adapt and pivot during the meeting as needed; and you successfully resolve all post-meeting item content edits.
  • Train and directly supervise Test Development Committee members in AP Japanese Language and Culture as content development contributors and reviewers. Recruit educators for the AP Japanese Language and Culture Development Committee and other opportunities to support AP Program.
  • Lead the successful scoring of student responses for AP Japanese Language and Culture Exams at the annual scoring event in person and online—the “AP Reading”—and produce AP Reading publications materials for teacher and student use. You plan all year, with increasing intensity in the months leading up to the Reading, ensuring all workflow steps for this incredibly complex event, as well as all post-Reading activities, are accounted for and successfully executed. 

Assessment Quality and Process (10-15%) 

  • Contribute to current research and best practices in assessment, and engage regularly with AP Curriculum & Assessment colleagues to align on standards and shared principles guiding AP’s assessment directions 
  • Support assessment workstreams within the AP English, World Languages, and Arts Department. 
  • Contribute to processes for efficient, high-quality assessment development. 
  • Contribute to initiatives to refine and improve question task models as well as exam design in collaboration with AP Curriculum & Assessment leaders and aligned to other College Board initiatives to achieve psychometric and disciplinary best practices on AP Japanese Language and Culture exams. 
  • Monitor exam validity, security, reliability, fairness, and quality, as well as reader reliability in accordance with established Program thresholds for AP Japanese Language and Culture exam, identifying areas for improvement and executing on targeted improvement initiatives. 
  • Collaborate with psychometrics and AP Curriculum & Assessment staff to establish fair, reliable, and valid cut scores for AP Japanese Language and Culture exam. 

 

Course Development, Program Support, and Stakeholder Engagement (5-25%) 

  • Refine and improve AP Japanese Language and Culture Framework to ensure clear and explicit learning outcomes that align with strategic priorities, including ensuring college/disciplinary standards as well as expanding the scope of reaching a broader audience of AP students.  
  • Collaborate with AP teams to support the development of new products for AP Japanese Language and Culture designed to address unmet teacher instructional needs, potentially including developing prototypes, participating in small-scale market-testing, and creating models for subsequent development in conjunction with other AP workstreams. 
  • Recruit educators for the AP Japanese Language and Culture Development Committee and other opportunities to support AP Program. 
  • Serve as a recognized and trusted resource within the educator community by collaboration and engagement with the community to drive teacher satisfaction with AP Japanese Language and Culture and its exam. 
  • Collaborate with the AP Professional learning team to support AP Japanese Language and Culture consultants and teachers. 
  • Work with the AP Higher Education team to co-develop and implement plans to raise college and university awareness of AP Japanese Language and Culture courses and exams, including recruiting college faculty to participate in the AP Reading, co-leading the planning and execution of discipline-specific AP Faculty Colloquia events, and supporting Visiting and Virtual Fellows Programs.  

About You

To qualify for this role, you must have:

  • A Master’s degree in Japanese Language or a directly related discipline, and knowledge of current trends in the discipline (required), although a doctorate in the discipline is strongly preferred  
  • Native to near-native fluency in Japanese.
  • Expertise in Japanese Language with at least 5 years of experience in standardized assessment development or related work; experience with digital assessment and teaching preferred 
  • Strong oral and written communication skills, with solid technical proficiency and a customer-focused mindset 
  • Excellent organizational and planning skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and maintain close attention to detail, including proofreading 
  • Demonstrated ability to implement processes and procedures, manage project plans and schedules, and maintain tracking documentation 
  • Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across all levels, and engage in giving and receiving constructive feedback 
  • Ability to travel 6-8 times per year, plus up to two additional weeks for the AP Reading; must be eligible to work in the United States 

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.


A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $96,000 - $135,000
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

Vous évoluerez au sein d'une product team Agile, dans une démarche où la stratégie de test ne repose plus sur l'écriture manuelle, mais sur l'orchestration d'agents et d'outils d'IA capables de générer une couverture de test à grande échelle.

Vous justifiez d'une solide expérience en QA / test automation et savez cadrer une IA pour produire un code de test pertinent - un bon test généré ne l'est que s'il est guidé par de solides patterns d'architecture.

  • Expérience significative des environnements Agile (Scrum / Kanban).

  • Sens de la qualité et de la non-régression.

About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a Software Engineer, AI Quality & Evaluation to build the engineering systems that help Bask Health test, evaluate, and improve AI-powered applications throughout their development and production lifecycles.

Bask Health supports direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses through a platform that connects patient experiences, merchant operations, clinical workflows, pharmacy coordination, and commerce tools. As we introduce more AI-powered capabilities across these areas, we need reliable software infrastructure that makes it easy for engineering teams to understand how those systems behave.

You'll help develop the internal tools, backend services, testing frameworks, and automation that support AI quality assurance across the platform.

This is a hands-on software engineering role focused on building reusable systems rather than evaluating individual models in isolation. You'll work with APIs, databases, automated testing infrastructure, model integrations, and developer tools to make AI evaluation more efficient, consistent, and accessible.

Your work may include evaluation execution services, test dataset management tools, automated regression pipelines, result comparison systems, and interfaces that help engineers investigate AI failures.

You'll collaborate with applied AI engineers, machine learning engineers, AI evaluation specialists, and backend engineers to understand their testing needs and translate those requirements into dependable software capabilities.

You'll also help integrate AI evaluation into normal engineering workflows. This includes making it easier to run tests during development, compare model or prompt changes, inspect failures, and identify regressions before production releases.

Because Bask operates in healthcare-related environments, you'll help ensure evaluation systems handle sensitive information appropriately, respect access permissions, and support testing for privacy, safety, and approved operational boundaries.

This position emphasizes strong software engineering fundamentals, developer experience, and production reliability. You'll contribute to technical architecture, write maintainable code, improve infrastructure performance, and own services that other engineering teams rely on.

We're looking for an engineer who enjoys building tools for other developers, understands the challenges of testing nondeterministic AI systems, and wants to create reliable infrastructure that improves software quality across the organization.

What You'll Do

  • Design, build, and maintain software infrastructure that supports AI quality and evaluation across Bask Health.
  • Develop backend services that execute and manage automated AI evaluations.
  • Build reusable testing tools for large language model applications.
  • Create APIs that allow engineering teams to submit evaluation jobs and retrieve results.
  • Develop systems for managing evaluation datasets, test cases, and expected outcomes.
  • Build automated workflows for comparing prompts, models, and application configurations.
  • Implement regression testing infrastructure for AI-powered features.

  • Build tools that help engineers inspect AI responses, failures, and test histories.
  • Implement structured result storage and comparison capabilities.
  • Develop internal dashboards or interfaces for reviewing evaluation outcomes.
  • Create reusable software libraries that simplify AI testing across multiple applications.
  • Build systems that support both deterministic checks and model-based evaluations.
  • Implement automated testing for tool-calling behavior and structured model outputs.
  • Develop infrastructure for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation applications.
  • Build asynchronous processing systems for large evaluation workloads.
  • Implement job scheduling, retries, timeouts, and error handling for evaluation services.
  • Develop monitoring and logging for evaluation infrastructure.
  • Optimize evaluation execution speed, reliability, and infrastructure costs.
  • Work with AI evaluation engineers to translate testing requirements into reusable software tools.
  • Collaborate with machine learning engineers to support model and prompt comparison workflows.
  • Implement appropriate access controls and secure handling of evaluation data.
  • Ensure evaluation infrastructure respects tenant boundaries and data privacy requirements.
  • Investigate infrastructure failures and resolve issues affecting evaluation reliability.
  • Improve developer documentation and internal tooling for AI testing.
  • Participate in code reviews, technical planning, and architecture discussions.
  • Own assigned AI quality engineering projects from design through deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, preferably in backend, platform, infrastructure, or developer tooling roles.
  • Experience building and maintaining production backend services.
  • Strong programming skills in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or comparable languages.
  • Experience designing and developing APIs and service integrations.
  • Familiarity with automated testing frameworks and software quality practices.
  • Understanding of continuous integration and deployment workflows.
  • Experience building reusable software components or internal engineering tools.
  • Familiarity with large language models and modern AI application development.
  • Understanding of the challenges involved in testing nondeterministic AI systems.
  • Experience working with relational databases and structured application data.
  • Familiarity with asynchronous processing and background job systems.
  • Understanding of distributed systems fundamentals and service reliability.
  • Experience developing automated testing pipelines.
  • Familiarity with cloud-based application deployment.
  • Understanding of authentication, authorization, and secure service communication.
  • Experience implementing logging, monitoring, and production diagnostics.
  • Ability to troubleshoot backend services and infrastructure issues.
  • Familiarity with configuration management and software release processes.
  • Experience writing maintainable, well-tested production code.
  • Understanding of API error handling, retries, and failure recovery.
  • Experience working with Git and collaborative engineering workflows.
  • Ability to translate technical requirements into reusable engineering systems.
  • Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with software engineers, AI engineers, and machine learning specialists.
  • Ability to independently own engineering projects from technical design through deployment.

Nice to Have

The role is driven by a genuine passion for improving the patient journey. It identifies where patients are delayed, missed or lost, partners with country medical and commercial teams to understand why, and turns those barriers into practical, compliant and measurable initiatives. This includes leading the integration of medical devices and diagnostic-enabling platforms (Florio, Enfuse, diagnostics) into patient journey frameworks for strategic CEERJ therapeutic areas (C3G/IC-MPGN, sHTG and secondarily haemophilia).

The role operates in a fast-moving, changing environment. The holder works in an agile way: sets few clear priorities, adapts quickly as launches, access and evidence evolve, and turns insight into executive-ready plans that are communicated clearly to the Brand Teams, Leadership Teams and Core Medical Team.

Main responsibilities:

Own the patient journey agenda for C3G/IC-MPGN and sHTG across CEERJ. Define, maintain and continuously refine a regional patient journey framework that identifies diagnostic difficulties, delays and post-therapy difficulties, and translates them into prioritized, measurable initiatives.

Partner with countries to map and clear barriers & opportunities. Work alongside country leaders and field teams to map country-specific barriers (awareness, testing access, laboratory and biopsy pathways, referral fragmentation, expert centre availability, non-pharmaceutical therapy optimization opportunities)

Build & resource executive plans. Develop concise, prioritized patient journey improvement projects with clear milestones, owners, dependencies and KPIs. Resource and adjust them rapidly as conditions change. Report progress to senior leadership in Core Medical Team, CEERJ LT and Brand Team forums.

Lead projects and matrix teams: drive relevant Patient Journey projects and allocated matrix teams from kick off to close out ensuring clear planning, budgeting, delivery and reporting on time and within budget

Lead integration of medical devices and enabling platforms. Lead integration of Florio, Enfuse, diagnostics and pipeline tools into patient journey frameworks across CEERJ. Ensure stakeholder value, country readiness and compliant use. Track adoption, escalate barriers and propose solutions.

Generate and act on patient journey insights. Interact with external community to enable systematic collection and synthesis of insights from HCPs, KOLs, diagnostic initiatives, patient organisations and country teams. Turn them into clear recommendations that change plans and decisions.

Mastery of the landscape. Keep current knowledge of C3G/IC-MPGN and sHTG science, diagnostic pathways, competitive and customer landscape, Tier 1 KOLs and patient advocacy groups, and related areas such as PNH and haemophilia.

Here at Sobi, our mission and culture get us excited to come to work every day.

Sobi is a global company with over 2000 employees in more than 30 countries and are committed to the societies where we operate. We are a specialised international biopharmaceutical company transforming the lives of people with rare and debilitating diseases, providing reliable access to innovative medicines in the areas of haematology, immunology, and specialty care. Sobi’s share is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. More about Sobi at sobi.com and LinkedIn.
We know our employees are our most valuable asset and our culture conveys that. We offer a competitive benefits package, to support the health and happiness of our staff.

Sobi Culture

At Sobi, we refuse to accept the status quo. This is because we have witnessed first-hand the challenges facing those affected by rare diseases and have used this knowledge to shape our business to find new ways of helping them.
As a specialized biopharmaceutical company, we are dedicated to rare diseases. And we see this focus as a strength. Accomplishing this requires strong partnerships with patients, partners and stakeholders across the entire value chain. Together, we define how our business can create solutions that serve the needs of those affected by rare diseases while facilitating sustainable growth.

At Sobi, each person brings their unique talents to work as a team and make a difference. We are dedicated to developing and delivering innovative therapies to improve the lives of rare disease patients and our edge comes from our team of people.

  • A strong testing mindset, with an appreciation for edge cases, validation, and the importance of verifying AI-generated code.
  • An understanding of secure development fundamentals, including input validation and protecting sensitive information in code, logs, and application workflows.

Web Designer

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S Business Hours

About the Role

We’re looking for a skilled Web Designer to create polished, user-centered web experiences that balance visual quality with usability. You’ll translate briefs and product goals into wireframes, mockups, and interactive prototypes, ensuring designs are responsive, consistent, and ready for development.

Working closely with developers and stakeholders, you’ll own your designs from initial concept through implementation review. This role is ideal for a detail-oriented designer who takes pride in their work, communicates proactively, and can manage projects independently in a remote, asynchronous environment.

What You’ll Own

Visual Design & Prototyping

  • Translate project briefs and product goals into clear, user-centered web designs.
  • Create wireframes, mockups, and interactive prototypes to communicate design concepts before development begins.
  • Balance visual appeal, usability, and business objectives across web experiences.

Responsive Web Design

  • Design and refine layouts for mobile, tablet, and desktop screens.
  • Apply responsive design principles to deliver consistent experiences across devices.
  • Consider how layouts and interactions translate into HTML and CSS.

Design System Maintenance

  • Contribute to and improve the existing design system.
  • Maintain consistency across components, typography, colors, spacing, and layouts.
  • Use component libraries and reusable design elements to support efficient workflows.

Developer Collaboration & Handoff

  • Work closely with front-end developers to ensure accurate design implementation.
  • Provide clear specifications, assets, and guidance for layouts and interactions.
  • Answer implementation questions and resolve design-related issues during development.

Feedback & Iteration

  • Incorporate stakeholder and user feedback into design revisions.
  • Refine designs efficiently while keeping the original project goals in focus.
  • Ask clarifying questions and communicate potential blockers early.

Design Quality Assurance

  • Review implemented pages against approved designs.
  • Identify visual inconsistencies, layout issues, and usability concerns.
  • Recommend fixes to maintain a high standard of design quality.

Required Experience & Skills

  • Professional experience in web design, supported by a portfolio demonstrating strong visual judgment, layout skills, and attention to detail.
  • Proficiency in a modern design tool such as Figma, Sketch, or Adobe XD.
  • Experience with component libraries, reusable components, and auto-layout workflows.
  • Solid understanding of responsive design principles and how designs translate into HTML and CSS.
  • Familiarity with UX fundamentals, including information architecture, user flows, accessibility, and usability.
  • Strong written and spoken English for clear communication with distributed teams and stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines independently.
  • Strong attention to detail and willingness to refine work based on feedback.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You take pride in producing polished, thoughtful design work and maintain high standards without constant supervision.
  • You communicate proactively, clarify requirements early, and keep collaborators informed.
  • You respond constructively to feedback and focus on delivering the best outcome for users and the business.
  • You work effectively in an asynchronous environment and manage your workload reliably.
  • You collaborate well with developers and understand the importance of accurate design handoffs.
  • You take ownership of your designs from concept through final implementation review.

What Success Looks Like

  • High-quality, user-centered web designs that align with project goals.
  • Responsive layouts that deliver consistent experiences across devices.
  • A well-maintained design system with reusable, consistent components.
  • Clear handoffs that help developers implement designs accurately.
  • Timely, thoughtful revisions based on feedback.
  • Implemented pages that closely match approved designs and meet quality expectations.

Typical Day

You’ll begin by reviewing feedback and comments on active design files and prioritizing your work. Depending on project needs, you may refine a landing page, develop a reusable design component, or revise a product interface.

You may also meet with a developer to discuss a design handoff or clarify an interaction. Later in the day, you’ll review completed work for quality, update project notes, and document progress so teammates across time zones can continue smoothly.

Interview Process

  • Initial Screening
  • Recruiter Interview
  • Client Interview
  • Offer & Onboarding

Redwood Automation Solution Designer (RunMyJobs / SAP BPA), SAP Finance Close, Norway

Contract: Duration being confirmed. Start: 15 November 2026. Location: Remote, for consultants based in Norway. Day rate: EUR 400 a day. Language: English.

The programme

An established organisation is automating its SAP finance close on the Redwood platform, the same engine that runs RunMyJobs and that SAP sold for years as SAP Central Process Scheduling (CPS) and SAP Business Process Automation (BPA). The work covers the record-to-report cycle: accruals, balance sheet reconciliation, journal posting and the period-end close, all driven into SAP S/4HANA and ECC.

You will own the solution design. You will work with the finance process owners to understand how the close runs today, decide what to automate and in what order, and set out a design the engineers can build on the Redwood platform. You will then stay with that design through build, testing and go-live, and make the calls when what was designed meets what is real.

What you will work on

Current-state analysis of the SAP period-end close with controllers and finance operations leads. The target automation design: close task lists, dependencies, calendars, approvals and exception paths, written up as the solution design. Accruals, balance sheet reconciliation and certification, and journal posting with its posting controls. The integration design with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and the other source systems, through APIs, files and middleware. Security and controls designed in: role-based access, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Monitoring, recovery and the non-functional design that keeps the close running. Leading the engineers through build, and reviewing what they deliver against the design at design-authority and go-live checkpoints. Test strategy and acceptance criteria with the finance users.

What you bring

Solution design on the Redwood platform under any of its names: RunMyJobs, SAP BPA by Redwood, SAP CPS or Cronacle. Design of an automated SAP FI/CO period-end close, where you ran the design workshops and wrote the design yourself. Controls built into your designs: role-based security, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Leading engineers from an approved design through build, testing and go-live. 8 or more years in SAP finance systems, finance automation or record-to-report process design.

Useful but not essential:

Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance). A BPA-to-RunMyJobs migration. CPS or Redwood tasks run from the SAP Financial Closing cockpit, or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. Financial services or another regulated industry.

How to respond

Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent Redwood or SAP close automation project: which Redwood product it ran on, the finance processes in scope, and which design decisions were yours.

About Yadimen

Yadimen Consulting Limited is an IT consulting company focused on financial services. For this programme we are putting experienced Redwood and SAP finance close automation people in front of the client.

A day in the life:

As a Creative Quality & Compliance Specialist, you’ll play an integral part in the overall quality and regulatory integrity of creative output across the Healthcare division, serving as the quality and compliance checkpoint within the creative production workflow. In this role, you’ll report directly to the Creative department and work alongside Creative Project Managers who own delivery timelines and task trafficking.

You will act as the gate through which every piece of creative passes before it reaches client Medical, Legal, and Regulatory (MLR) reviewers and again before it goes live. You'll review ads, landing pages, emails, social content, and video for MLR regulatory compliance, brand and design standards, and copy accuracy. Additionally, you’ll operate hands-on inside Veeva Vault PromoMats—managing claims, annotations, references, and submission packages—while building and refining the quality standards the creative team works against to raise the bar across the healthcare portfolio.

  • Pre-Submission Compliance QA: Review all creative assets against MLR requirements — claims accuracy, fair balance, ISI placement, reference linking, branded vs. unbranded vs. disease-awareness rules — before they enter client Medical, Legal, and Regulatory review.
  • Post-Approval Launch QA: Final quality proof of approved assets — landing pages, ads, emails, creative — before they go live, confirming that approved content was implemented correctly and no errors were introduced in production.
  • Veeva Vault PromoMats Operations: Own the hands-on Veeva workflow — annotating assets, entering and linking claims, managing references, tracking submission status, and packaging 2253 filings.
  • Brand & Design Standards Enforcement: Review creative output for visual consistency, spec adherence, and style guide compliance across all healthcare client deliverables.
  • Copy Quality Review: Review all copy for grammar, tone, messaging accuracy, and alignment with approved claims and client brand voice.
  • QA Process Documentation & Refinement: Build, maintain, and continuously improve the quality and compliance standards, checklists, and review processes the creative team follows.
  • Creative Workflow Coordination: Support creative production operations alongside the Creative Project Manager and Account PM — maintaining Asana boards and deliverable trackers, communicating timelines and managing feedback cycles with client stakeholders, trafficking tasks between the creative team and client POCs, coordinating with cross-channel PMs on shared deliverables, and organizing client-provided assets within Power Digital’s file structure.
  • Employ AI technologies to enhance and optimize business processes.

  • Other applicable or related duties as assigned.

Role Requirements:

  • 4+ years in healthcare or pharmaceutical creative production, agency or in-house, with direct exposure to MLR review workflows
  • Demonstrated understanding of FDA OPDP guidance and 21 CFR 202, including fair balance, ISI placement, branded vs. unbranded vs. disease-awareness content rules, and 2253 filing requirements
  • Veeva Vault PromoMats experience (annotating, claims management, submission tracking) highly preferred
  • Strong eye for brand consistency, design quality, and copy accuracy across digital formats (paid social, display, landing pages, email)

  • Documented QA standards maintained and current across all supported accounts

Most Important Things (MITs)

  • Establish the pre-submission and pre-launch QA checkpoints as defined, repeatable stages in the creative workflow.
  • Own the Veeva PromoMats workflow for assigned accounts — claims, annotations, references, and submissions operating cleanly from day one.
  • Build and maintain the QA standards documentation (checklists, compliance reference guides, brand review criteria) the creative team works against.

  • Own kernel driver signing: You run the end-to-end signing process for our Windows kernel drivers, including EV code signing, Microsoft Partner Center attestation, and HLK/WHQL submissions where needed. You keep the pipeline compliant with Microsoft’s driver signing requirements as they change.
  • Package for the enterprise: You build and maintain MSI, MSIX, and Win32 (.intunewin) packages for Intune deployment. You define install and uninstall logic, detection rules, dependencies, silent installs, and upgrade paths that IT teams can roll out to thousands of devices without a single support ticket.
  • Manage the certificate lifecycle: You own every certificate the product relies on: code signing, driver signing, root and intermediate certificates for TLS inspection, and device and service certificates. You handle issuance, secure storage in HSMs or key vaults, distribution, rotation, renewal, and revocation, with zero surprise expiries.
  • Automate signing and release: You integrate signing and packaging into CI/CD so every release is signed, versioned, and reproducible. No manual steps on someone’s laptop and no private keys in places they should not be.
  • Enable customer deployments: You write the deployment guides, Intune configuration profiles, and certificate trust policies that customer IT teams follow. You join calls with their endpoint teams to troubleshoot rollouts when needed.
  • Own reliability in the field: You track deployment success rates, failed installs, and signing or trust errors across the install base, and you fix root causes, not symptoms.

Requirements

  • Seasoned Windows systems engineer: 5+ years of experience in Windows systems engineering, endpoint engineering, or build and release for Windows software. You know the Windows installer stack, services, the registry, and the certificate stores inside out.
  • Driver signing experience: You have signed and shipped Windows kernel drivers in production through Microsoft’s attestation or WHQL process. You understand EV certificates, cross-signing history, and what Secure Boot and HVCI require.
  • Hands-on Intune packaging: You have packaged and deployed software through Microsoft Intune at enterprise scale, including Win32 apps, MSI/MSIX, detection rules, and configuration profiles. SCCM/MECM experience is a plus.
  • PKI and certificate management: You have managed certificate lifecycles in production, using tools such as Azure Key Vault, HSMs, internal CAs, or certificate management platforms. You can explain a chain of trust to a developer and to a customer’s security team.
  • Automation mindset: You script with PowerShell and have built signing or packaging steps into CI/CD pipelines such as GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps.
  • Clear communicator: You can walk a US enterprise IT team through a deployment in plain English, and you write documentation people actually follow.

jobs.excerpt: Who We AreYellow Card is the largest licensed Stablecoin-based infrastructure provider operating across over 60 countries.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Yellow Card is the largest licensed Stablecoin-based infrastructure provider operating across over 60 countries. From Stablecoin payment infrastructure to fiat settlement rails, wallet services, and custom local Stablecoin issuance, Yellow Card provides the complete infrastructure businesses need to manage Stablecoins, payments, and operations across 50 emerging markets.

Yellow Card operates with a substantial global team spanning 24 countries. This workforce is characterized by its linguistic diversity, with collective speaking of over 25 languages, underscoring the company’s extensive international reach.

The Security Operations Engineer is the operational backbone of the Security Operations Centre (SOC). It is a fully remote, hands-on, technical role that owns three tightly integrated domains: security alert design, triaging, and automated response; cloud security posture management across EKS and AWS environments; and posture tracking and reporting.

Reporting to the Associate Director, Product & Infrastructure Security, the engineer works alongside a mature Application Security team and collaborates closely with DevOps, Engineering, and Security GRC functions. The role sits within the First Line of Defense and is expected to progressively drive down manual effort through detection-as-code and SOAR automation.

This is not a perimeter-security or scan-and-report role. The right candidate must be comfortable writing detection logic, triaging cloud misconfigurations at the infrastructure level, and owning end-to-end vulnerability remediation cycles in containerised environments.

What You'll Do

1. Security Operations

The engineer owns the full lifecycle of security detection and response inside the SOC, from signal design through to automated containment. This is the primary domain of the role.

Alert design and coverage

  • Design and maintain SIEM detection rules covering cloud, container, identity, and application layers, using both signature-based and behavioural logic
  • Map detection coverage against the MITRE ATT&CK framework and identify gaps relevant to the organisation's AWS and EKS attack surface
  • Integrate threat intelligence feeds to refresh rule logic for emerging threats and TTPs
  • Maintain a detection backlog, prioritised by risk, with defined review cadences

Alert triage

  • Daily SIEM alert triage following defined response timing standard
  • Classify, investigate, and resolve security signals;
  • Reduce false-positive rates through structured tuning cycles, with documented rationale for rule changes
  • Maintain triage runbooks for key production detection rules

Automated response workflows (SOAR)

  • Build and maintain SOAR playbooks for common alert types including IAM anomalies, misconfiguration alerts, exposed secrets, and container runtime events
  • Automate enrichment steps (asset lookup, threat intel correlation, ownership resolution) to reduce analyst time-to-context
  • Document automation logic and maintain version control for all playbooks
  • Measure and report automation coverage rate as a standing KRI

2. Cloud Security Posture Management

Cloud posture management is the infrastructure-facing domain of the role, covering vulnerability management, identity governance, and configuration and change control. AWS EKS and Serverless resources are the primary environments.

Vulnerability management

  • Own the end-to-end vulnerability triage process for cloud and container environments, prioritising findings by business impact using CVSS scoring, asset criticality, and exploitability context
  • Manage EKS-specific vulnerability coverage: base image currency, workload scanning results, pod security standards compliance, and node group patching cadence
  • Coordinate remediation with engineering teams by opening well-scoped tickets, tracking progress, and escalating SLA breaches
  • Maintain MTTR and SLA compliance data by severity tier
  • Oversee CSPM posture score targets; triage new Critical findings within defined SLA windows

Identity and access governance

  • Review and approve IAM policy changes, enforcing least-privilege and flagging over-permissioned roles or service accounts
  • Execute scheduled IAM hygiene reviews: unused credentials, stale access keys, overly broad policies, and cross-account trust boundaries
  • Govern workload identity configurations in EKS, ensuring service accounts carry only the permissions required
  • Support the secrets rotation program and enforce zero hardcoded credentials across the estate

Configuration and change management

  • Review and approve cloud network security changes: security group modifications, network ACL changes, and routing updates
  • Own container image security: base image update cadence, scanning results review, and image ownership classification
  • Investigate and remediate misconfiguration alerts surfaced by CSPM tooling within defined SLA windows
  • Maintain a configuration baseline for critical cloud resources and flag drift

3. Posture Tracking and Reporting

The engineer is the primary data owner for security posture metrics across both SOC and cloud domains. Reporting outputs feed executive dashboards, GRC compliance evidence, and quarterly risk reviews.

KRI data collection

  • Collect and maintain Key Risk Indicator data across all three KRA domains on defined cadences
  • SOC KRIs: MTTA (Mean Time to Acknowledge), MTTR, false-positive rate, automation coverage rate, detection coverage score
  • VM KRIs: Critical/High finding counts, SLA compliance rate by severity, MTTR by tier, overdue remediation count
  • Posture KRIs: CSPM score, under-protected asset count, misconfiguration closure rate, IAM hygiene score, log source coverage

Recurring control reviews

  • Execute infrastructure security control checks on weekly (CSPM critical findings), monthly (IAM hygiene, secrets rotation status), and quarterly (posture benchmark, detection coverage review) cadences
  • Produce structured findings reports for each review cycle, flagging control failures for escalation

Reporting

  • Provide SOC and cloud posture metrics, including trends, at the required reporting cycles
  • Support external audit and due diligence processes by providing evidence artefacts

4. Others

  • Co-own the shared vulnerability backlog (infrastructure side) with the Application Security team, ensuring consistent prioritisation methodology across domains
  • Serve as the infrastructure and identity SME for the AppSec team during application security assessments and architecture reviews
  • Own infrastructure containment during incidents that span application and infrastructure layers, working alongside AppSec for root cause analysis
  • Provide infrastructure, identity, and network security review for new third-party integrations prior to deployment
  • Collaborate with the Security GRC function on control evidence and compliance mapping, particularly for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and GDPR requirements

What You'll Bring

  • Fluency in English, both written and verbal
  • Ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and across different time zones
  • 3 to 5 years of experience in security operations, cloud security, or infrastructure security engineering
  • Hands-on AWS security experience: IAM policy design, virtual network architecture, cloud-native security services, CloudTrail, GuardDuty
  • Kubernetes and EKS security experience: pod security standards, network policy enforcement, workload identity, image scanning
  • SIEM operations: alert triage, detection rule authoring (signature-based and behavioural), log analysis and correlation
  • Vulnerability management: CSPM tooling, risk-based prioritisation, CVSS scoring, SLA framework operation
  • IaC security: ability to read and review Terraform or CloudFormation for misconfigurations
  • Incident response: investigation, containment, and post-incident reporting
  • Experience in a regulated environment (FinTech, payments, banking, or crypto preferred)
  • Ability to author and tune detection rules without relying on vendor-supplied defaults
  • Structured written communication for triage reports, post-incident write-ups, and stakeholder metrics
  • Ability to coordinate remediation across engineering teams without direct authority
  • Comfort operating in a lean team where domain boundaries are broader than in large enterprise security functions
  • Professional certifications: AWS Security Specialty (highly valued)
  • Experience with CSPM and SIEM platforms: Datadog, Wiz, Orca Security
  • Experience with secrets management platforms: AWS Secrets Manager
  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks: SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, DORA
  • Scripting ability in Python or Bash for detection-as-code and operational automation
  • Experience with SOAR or workflow automation platforms
  • Understanding of cryptocurrency or blockchain security considerations
  • Experience in a startup or scale-up environment
  • AI tooling familiarity and interest in applying AI to operational workflows

What We Offer

  • Compensation & Benefits: We offer competitive compensation and meaningful health coverage, and all full-time employees are participants in our stock option plan.
  • Learning & Development: Access to resources, support, and autonomy to grow professionally.
  • Remote-First Flexibility: We embrace a fully remote work environment.
  • Regulated, multi-geography environment with real-world impact on financial inclusion
  • Mental Health Support Services: Your mental well-being matters to us.
  • Ownership of the SOC and cloud security posture function from day one, in a high-growth FinTech environment
  • Broad domain exposure: detection engineering, cloud security, container security, incident response, and compliance
  • Collaborative team culture with a mature AppSec function and strong leadership support

Ready to Join Us?

Are you up for the challenge? Apply today and be part of shaping the future of FinTech. Let's innovate, disrupt, and lead together!

You’ll join a collaborative, global team pushing the boundaries of scientific innovation. Your ideas and efforts will have a tangible impact, accelerating scientific progress and discovery. We offer a dynamic, remote-friendly environment that fosters high integrity and collaboration, empowering you to excel. Dotmatics is a company built by scientists, for scientists. Combined, we are now the world’s largest cloud-based scientific research R&D platform. We need your help to keep growing and pioneering the future.

We are Science Driven. We are Customer Centric. We are Better Together.

What do we need

Dotmatics is seeking a DevOps Engineer to join our team working on ground-breaking Scientific Software products such as Luma. In this role, you will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge to help improve our processes, infrastructure and security by applying best practices with the latest technologies. You will be AI fluent and know how AI influences engineering and DevOps

In this role you will get to:

  • Design and manage CI/CD and deployment pipelines for both AWS-native and Kubernetes-based applications
  • Provide advice/assistance to the product teams, clarifying requirements for deployment
  • Collaborate with product teams on cloud and container best practices
  • Manage IT infrastructure in cloud computing environments
  • Automation: Use CI tools to automate code changes, builds, testing, and analysis
  • Monitoring: Monitor performance after release
  • Develop and improve monitoring systems for automated alerts
  • Strategy: Design and manage the DevOps infrastructure, pipelines, and processes
  • SECURITY: Embed security into every stage of the delivery lifecycle (DevSecOps), including automated SAST, DAST, dependency, secrets, and container image scanning in CI/CD pipelines
  • SECURITY: Implement and enforce least-privilege IAM, network segmentation, encryption in transit and at rest, and secrets management (e.g. AWS Secrets Manager, Vault, KMS)
  • SECURITY: Harden Kubernetes clusters and cloud environments using policy-as-code, admission controls, runtime protection, and CIS/NIST benchmarks
  • SECURITY: Support vulnerability management, incident response, audit readiness, and compliance efforts (e.g. SOC 2, ISO 27001)
  • AI: Use AI-assisted tooling to accelerate pipeline development, infrastructure code, troubleshooting, and incident analysis
  • AI: Apply AI/ML-driven capabilities to monitoring, including anomaly detection, alert noise reduction, and automated root-cause analysis
  • AI: Build and operate deployment pipelines and infrastructure for AI/ML and LLM-based workloads, including model serving, GPU-enabled clusters, and cost controls
  • AI: Establish guardrails for responsible AI use in engineering workflows, including data privacy, access controls, and review of AI-generated code and configuration

We are looking for people who have 8+ years of experience maintaining high-traffic applications and complex technical infrastructure. You will be someone with a proven background in supporting cloud environments, with hands-on experience translating AWS Well-Architected principles into action.

The key skills we are looking for:

  • Kubernetes clusters/customer cloud environments
  • AWS (ECS, EKS, ALB, EC2, S3, RDS, CloudFront, Route53, etc.)
  • Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi)
  • CI/CD tools (Octopus Deploy, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, TeamCity, CodePipeline, etc.)
  • APMs and logging (e.g. Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, ELK, App Insights)
  • Networking concepts in cloud environments
  • Software development lifecycle processes/version control
  • Security: DevSecOps practices, AWS security services (IAM, GuardDuty, Security Hub, WAF, Config, KMS), container and supply chain security (image signing, SBOMs), and security scanning tools (e.g. Trivy, Snyk, SonarQube, Checkov)
  • Security: Familiarity with Kubernetes security (RBAC, network policies, Pod Security Standards, OPA/Kyverno) and secrets management
  • AI: Practical experience using AI coding and operations assistants (e.g. GitHub Copilot, Claude, Amazon Q) to improve engineering productivity
  • AI: Understanding of how to deploy and operate AI/ML workloads (e.g. Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, model-serving on Kubernetes) and observe their performance and cost
  • AI: Awareness of AI-specific risks such as prompt injection, data leakage, and insecure AI-generated code

You may also have:

  • Scripting languages (e.g. Python, Bash)
  • Linux administration and networking (e.g. HTTP/2)
  • Microservice and serverless architectures
  • Experience with GitOps tooling (e.g. Argo CD, Flux)
  • Experience building internal tooling or agents that apply AI to DevOps workflows (e.g. automated incident triage, ChatOps)
  • Relevant certifications (e.g. AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, AWS Security Specialty, CKA/CKS)
  • Databases (e.g. PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB)
  • Exposure to AI-enabled tooling or workflows, with openness to incorporating AI into day-to-day work

Research shows us the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting outstanding candidates, so please don’t hesitate to apply — we’d love to hear from you.

By submitting your application, you agree that Dotmatics may collect your personal data for recruiting, global organization planning, and related purposes. Dotmatics Privacy Notice explains what personal information we may process, where we may process your personal information, our purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over Dotmatics use of your personal information.

Dotmatics is an equal opportunity employer. We are a welcoming place for everyone, and we do our best to make sure all people feel supported and connected at work.

jobs.excerpt: “I am hugely excited about my future and the future of CyberOne.
jobs.description:
“I am hugely excited about my future and the future of CyberOne. I have enjoyed my time here immensely and have learnt a huge amount in a short space of time, year-for-year I've learnt more here than I have at Microsoft and PwC.” - CyberOne Consultant

About CyberOne

CyberOne is a pure-play Microsoft security partner dedicated to helping enterprises realise the full value of the Microsoft Security portfolio—across Defender XDR, Sentinel, Entra, Purview, Intune, Copilot for Security and more. We combine deep technical expertise with outcome-driven services that accelerate secure cloud adoption, modernise threat protection and simplify compliance.

Job Title:Head of Incident Response

Location:Remote

Employment Type:Full time

Role purpose

The Head of Incident Response is accountable for the management, quality and continual improvement of CyberOne’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) Cyber Incident Response (CIR) Standard Level service.

The role ensures that Cyber Incident Response Leads have the direction, tools, processes and support needed to deliver effective retained customer onboarding, incident response engagements and preparedness activities.

Alongside service leadership, the Head of Incident Response retains an active operational capability, supporting concurrent engagements and contributing directly where incidents require additional leadership, technical expertise or response capacity.

Responsibilities

Service ownership and quality

  • Own the operational delivery of the NCSC CREST accredited CIR service, ensuring clear standards for customer onboarding, incident management, investigation, reporting and post-incident review.
  • Oversee CIR Lead performance during engagements, providing direction and support to ensure delivery meets agreed scope, service commitments and client expectations.
  • Ensure the team has appropriate tools, documentation, playbooks and processes to deliver the service effectively.
  • Oversee the quality assurance of investigation reports and client deliverables, ensuring conclusions are supported by evidence, limitations are clearly explained and recommendations are practical and prioritised.
  • Use engagement feedback, lessons learned and changes in the threat landscape to identify and implement service improvements.
  • Report service performance, capacity constraints, delivery risks and improvement priorities to the Operations Director.

Operational leadership and client engagement

  • Maintain oversight of active engagements, identifying incidents that require additional support, management intervention or escalation.
  • Participate directly in complex incidents and support concurrent engagements, providing incident leadership and technical assistance as required.
  • Support CIR Leads with difficult response decisions, executive communications and sensitive client situations.
  • Take ownership of IR client technical escalations and seek resolutions with the best interests of both parties.
  • Assist with scoping IR engagements, clarifying client needs, delivery requirements, dependencies and service limitations.
  • Meet newly signed clients with the assigned CIR lead to introduce the service, establish expectations and support an effective transition into onboarding.
  • Ensure retained customer onboarding is completed to an appropriate standard and that the team can identify and communicate gaps affecting response readiness.

People and resource management

  • Directly manage, support and develop the CIR Leads, promoting consistent delivery, effective collaboration and knowledge sharing.
  • Assess current and anticipated demand against team capacity, identifying gaps in coverage, capability and resilience.
  • Prepare business cases for additional hiring and support interviews and candidate assessment following approval.
  • Work with the SecOps Manager to coordinate additional SecOps support, ensuring resource allocation considers the continued delivery of the MXDR service.
  • Support the development of SecOps team members who contribute to incident response, agreeing training and participation with their management.
  • Monitor workload and support effective cover and handovers during prolonged or concurrent engagements.

Essential professional requirements

  • Demonstrable experience leading significant cyber security incidents, including complex investigations, multidisciplinary response teams and senior stakeholder communications.
  • Experience managing or overseeing a client-facing incident response capability, with responsibility for delivery quality and service improvement.
  • Ability to communicate confidently with executive and board-level stakeholders, translating technical findings into business impact, response options and decisions.
  • Strong client management skills, including resolving escalations and maintaining constructive relationships during disruptive or sensitive incidents.
  • Ability to lead and develop experienced responders while providing appropriate challenge, support and direction.
  • Strong judgement when prioritising competing engagements and balancing incident response requirements against wider operational commitments.
  • Experience assessing resource requirements and presenting clear, evidence-based business cases to senior management.
  • Excellent written communication and quality assurance skills, including reviewing incident reports, executive summaries and remediation recommendations.
  • Professional discretion and sound judgement when handling sensitive information, investigation evidence and uncertain findings.

Essential technical requirements

  • Strong practical experience responding to incidents such as ransomware, business email compromise, identity compromise, malware infections and suspected data exfiltration.
  • Ability to contribute directly to investigations and response activities, alongside providing technical oversight and incident leadership.
  • Ability to assess and challenge investigative findings, identify evidence gaps and direct analysis to establish incident scope, attack progression and business impact.
  • Strong understanding of enterprise environments, including Windows, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365, cloud services and common network technologies.
  • Experience using SIEM, EDR and identity telemetry to investigate and correlate activity across endpoints, accounts and cloud services.
  • Understanding of attacker techniques involving credential theft, session compromise, persistence, privilege escalation, lateral movement and command-and-control communications.
  • Ability to assess containment, eradication and recovery options, considering business dependencies, operational consequences, evidence preservation and client approval requirements.
  • Understanding of secure evidence handling and chain-of-custody principles, including recognising when specialist forensic support is required.
  • Ability to assess how telemetry coverage, retention and licensing limitations affect response readiness, investigative confidence and conclusions.
  • Practical understanding of incident response guidance and threat frameworks, particularly NIST SP 800-61 and MITRE ATT&CK.

Desirable experience and qualifications

  • Experience managing incident response delivery within a consultancy or managed security service provider.
  • Experience with Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender XDR and KQL, alongside familiarity with other enterprise security platforms.
  • Experience developing incident response services, delivery processes, playbooks and quality standards.
  • Experience delivering preparedness workshops, tabletop exercises and incident response plan reviews.
  • Experience coordinating with legal advisers, cyber insurers, specialist forensic providers and crisis communications teams.
  • Awareness of data protection and regulatory considerations, including recognising when clients require specialist legal or privacy advice.
  • Relevant qualifications such as GCIH, GCFA, CISSP or CISM. Equivalent practical experience is equally valued.
  • ITIL 4 knowledge or certification, particularly in relation to incident, problem and change management.

Accountability and authority

The Head of Incident Response owns the operational management, delivery standards and continual improvement of the IR service. CIR Leads remain responsible for leading their assigned engagements, supported by the Head where additional oversight or operational assistance is required.

jobs.description:
Enlighten, honored as a Top Workplace from USA Today, is a leader in big data solution development and deployment, with expertise in cloud-based services, software and systems engineering, cyber capabilities, and data science. Enlighten provides continued innovation and proactivity in meeting our customers’ greatest challenges.

We recognize that the most effective environment for your projects doesn’t always look the same. Our hybrid work approach ensures that you can make lasting relationships with your team and collaborate in-person to get the job done—while having the flexibility to work from home when needed to achieve focused results.

Why Enlighten?

At Enlighten, our team’s unwavering work ethic, top talent and celebration of innovative ideas have helped us thrive. We know that our employees are essential to our company’s success, so we seek to take care of you as much as you take care of us. Here are a few highlights of our benefits package:
• 100% paid employee premium for healthcare, vision and dental plans.
• 10% 401k benefit.
• Generous PTO + 10 paid holidays.

• Education/training allowances.

Anticipated Salary Range: $143,507.00 - $245,000.00. The salary range for this role is intended as a good faith estimate based on the role's location, expectations, and responsibilities. When extending an offer, Enlighten takes a variety of factors into consideration which include, but are not limited to, the role's function, internal equity and a candidate's education or training, work experience, certifications and key skills. Occasionally positions/roles may include additional non-recurrent compensation and will be addressed by the recruiter during the interview process.

Job Description

We build and operate critical backend systems that manage trillions of records, ingest billions of new records daily, and service hundreds of thousands of queries per day across the Department of Defense (DoD). Our team values getting things done efficiently, fostering a low-ego environment, and empowering our engineers with autonomy.

In this role, you'll be a key contributor to designing, building, and scaling this core infrastructure. You will tackle a diverse set of challenges, from developing robust API endpoints and modifying complex open-source systems like Trino, to architecting intricate identity federation solutions, managing large-scale data ingest, and streamlining our deployment automation. If you are a mature, pragmatic, and highly skilled developer who thrives on flexibility and making a tangible impact with minimal bureaucratic overhead, we want to talk to you.

#Mid-Senior Level

Essential Job Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain complex, scalable, and critical backend systems and services capable of handling massive data volumes and high query loads.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 15+ years of experience as a software engineer, designing, developing, and deploying complex backend systems and a Bachelors in related field or 13 years experience with Masters; or High School Diploma and 19 years experience.

  • Experience working with or modifying Trino (or similar distributed SQL query engines).
  • Experience with containerization and orchestration, particularly Kubernetes.
  • Familiarity with PostgreSQL or similar relational databases.
  • A drive for pragmatic solutions with a strong bias for action and a "get stuff done" mentality.
  • Possess a low-ego and collaborative approach to teamwork and technical discussions.
  • Self-motivated and thrive in a low-process, high-autonomy environment, working effectively with minimal supervision.
  • Highly adaptable and a quick learner, comfortable context-switching and rapidly mastering new technologies and diverse technical domains such as API development, complex open-source modification, identity federation protocols, large-scale data ingest, and deployment automation.

jobs.description:
Description

Position: Credit Analyst / Para-Broker (End-to-End Loan Processor)

Salary: Php 80,000 - 160,000 (Salary will be based depending on the candidate's experience)

Working Hours & Conditions: Full Time (Independent Contractor Arrangement) , Will follow Queensland business hours

Holidays:TBC

ABOUT THE COMPANY:

The client is a mortgage brokerage company that has been operating since 2010. With a background in complex self employed and investor lending and structure, they focus now on individual, tailored solutions to help people buy their dream home. They take time with clients to uncover solutions, educate, and provide long term support. The client does currently does all of the credit analysis and processing himself and wants to step back from it so he can focus on clients, marketing, referrals and growing the business. The role exists to support the broker and clients by lifting productivity and releasing the broker's time to bring in more business.

Role Overview

This is an end-to-end credit analyst and loan processor, a hybrid of credit analyst and para-broker. It is a senior role: the person takes a file from first document through to settlement, working out the client's position and the best strategy, preparing lending proposals, packaging and lodging applications, and keeping clients updated. They should be able to own the work, give advice on how to structure it, and run it without close direction. This role will be the template for the future team, and it will be replicated over time to build redundancy.

Key Responsibilities

Pre-Credit Assessment

  • Collect, check and file supporting documents in Google Drive using the company naming format
  • Verify and update the Mercury Fact Find from supporting documents, and update Mercury and BrokerEngine with client details
  • Download and examine Equifax reports through Mercury, and examine the MLE
  • Verify property estimates using RPData, and order AVMs where equity is critical
  • Request missing, outstanding or extra documents needed to complete the assessment

Credit Research & Strategy

  • Complete Quickli servicing from the Fact Find and documents, and complete the Funding Position and Preliminary Assessment in BrokerEngine
  • Identify information to confirm, actions the client must take, policies to review and key strategies to improve the client's position
  • Assess current and future ability to reach the client's goal, and record capacity, limitations, options and the recommended strategy

Lending Proposals

  • Complete the Research form, list policy hurdles and potential lenders, confirm policies with lenders and shortlist
  • Run pricing requests and escalations, and order valuations and update security details
  • Complete the Product Comparison, Funding Position and Mudmap, and select lenders based on policy, servicing and cost
  • Create the Loan Strategy Proposal document and save everything to the client file

Loan Processing & Submission

  • Complete broker notes and generate the PDF for submission, prepare Mercury and compliance documents, and finalise Mercury for lodgement
  • Prepare AOL (and LoanApp), review and approve documents, and ensure accuracy before submitting
  • Get application and compliance forms signed, collect outstanding documents and submit to the lender

Approvals, AIPs, Construction & Settlement

  • Review approval conditions against funding positions, update key dates and the document portal, and update solicitors on formal approval
  • Convert AIPs to formal approvals, ordering valuations and updating the funding position
  • Handle construction loans: cost analysis, insurance, warranty, contracts, council-approved plans, progress payments and building insurance at handover
  • After approval, check the loan agreement against the approved product, send signing instructions and disbursement details, and record loan and offset details
  • At settlement, generate the settlement advice, email the client from the template, update records, archive the file and prepare the review

Client Communication & Daily Responsibilities

  • Keep clients updated using the BrokerEngine email and SMS templates: every 2 days at initial assessment, daily at signing and from lodgement to approval, and immediately on status changes
  • Complete Preliminary Assessments (Your Home Plans) and Loan Strategy Proposals as they are ready, and action MIRs within one business day
  • Clarify credit questions with the broker when required, and keep the BrokerEngine checklist up to date
  • Manage individual and shared inboxes, action items within one business day, and chase clients for outstanding information
  • Build and maintain the company's process guides, working with the broker

What Success Looks Like

  • Manages 5 to 7 client lodgements t settlements a month, and processes an additional 5 Your Home Plans a month
  • Frees the broker for client conversations, marketing and lead generation, client reviews and workshopping with clients
  • Keeps the business running smoothly when the broker is away or focused elsewhere
  • Leaves time to explore productivity improvements as the team grows

Requirements

Non-negotiable

  • 3 to 5+ years' experience as a credit analyst or para-broker in an Australian mortgage brokerage
