jobs.excerpt: Location: 100% remote within the U. S.  (any U. S.
jobs.description:
Location: 100% remote within the U.S. (any U.S. time zone)

Classification: Full-time, non-exempt employee

Salary: $24.95 - $35.07 per hour

Welcome to Miaplaza!

Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive homeschool curriculum platform where all students can be successful!MiaPrep Online High School (MOHS) is our online high school for students in grades 7-12. Formed in 2022 and accredited in 2023, we’ve grown from 80 students in our first year to over 530 in 2025! Miaplaza’s leadership aims to continue this high-growth trajectory, with a goal of serving 10,000+ students in the next 5-10 years! 🚀

Role Summary

The Academic Counselor partners with students and families in grades 7-12 to support academic success, graduation completion, and postsecondary readiness. The Academic Counselor acts as a case manager providing proactive academic planning, targeted intervention, and relationship-based support to ensure students remain engaged, on track, and progressing toward their goals.

Academic Counselors focus on high-impact, student-facing work, academic decision-making, graduation oversight, postsecondary planning, and whole-child academic support - while collaborating closely with Advisors, Student Support Specialists, Teachers, and the Registrar.

Academic Counselors are expected to spend approximately 45–50% of their work week (18–20 hours per week) in direct and indirect student-facing activities, including student and family meetings, academic planning conversations, proactive outreach, and intervention.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

Academic Planning & Graduation Oversight

  • Develop and maintain individualized academic plans aligned to graduation requirements and student goals

  • Monitor academic progress toward graduation and intervene when students fall off track

  • Lead student-specific graduation pathway planning and course sequencing decisions

  • Ensure students meet graduation eligibility requirements

  • Read and interpret incoming transcripts, including from nontraditional, out-of-state, or international systems, and translate them accurately into MOHS courses, credit, and SAP

Student Intervention & Case Management

  • Serve as the primary Tier 2 intervention point for students escalated by Advisors

  • Conduct targeted counseling conversations to identify barriers to academic progress

  • Develop and implement short-term academic intervention plans

  • Coordinate support across Advisors, Student Support Specialists, Teachers, and administrative teams

  • Monitor intervention outcomes and adjust plans as needed

  • Hold firm boundaries around academic policy and eligibility requirements when needed, while keeping the conversation supportive and counselor-forward

Student & Family Engagement

  • Build and maintain strong, trust-based relationships with students and families

  • Facilitate proactive and responsive parent–student–counselor meetings

  • Serve as a consistent point of contact for complex academic planning conversations

  • Communicate clearly and collaboratively to support student persistence

Postsecondary Planning & Curriculum Alignment

  • Guide students and families in postsecondary planning, including college, career, and alternative pathways

  • Ensure academic coursework, pacing, and graduation plans align with postsecondary goals

  • Provide accurate guidance on graduation requirements and future readiness

Onboarding & Enrollment

  • Lead new family academic onboarding conversations

  • Partner with the Registrar to ensure accurate records review, course placement and scheduling execution

  • Support students through key transitions, including entry, re-entry, and graduation

Whole-Child Academic Perspective

  • Apply a whole-child lens to academic planning, recognizing external factors that impact learning and engagement

  • Integrate wellness considerations into academic decision-making without providing clinical mental health treatment

  • Support students in developing self-advocacy, goal-setting, and executive functioning skills

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for mental health-related concerns escalated by staff: assess academic impact, develop a support plan, and refer to internal or external resources as needed — while holding a firm boundary against providing therapy, ongoing counseling, or diagnosis

Student Safety & Compliance

  • Provide consultation and academic follow-up after safety protocols are enacted

  • Maintain appropriate documentation and professional boundaries

  • All MOHS staff are considered mandated reporters and are required to respond to student safety and mental health concerns in accordance with the MOHS Crisis Response SOP. This includes participating in required training and, when appropriate, administering the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) and following all documentation and escalation procedures.

Collaboration & Systems Work

  • Collaborate closely with Advisors to clarify escalation pathways and intervention roles

  • Partner with Student Support Specialists on Tier 3 referrals and transitions

  • Work with the Registrar to ensure accurate records and smooth operational handoffs

  • Contribute to the development, documentation, and refinement of counseling SOPs

  • Support consistent implementation of counseling processes while maintaining flexibility for student needs

Comprehensive Counseling Program & Pathway Development

  • Contribute to the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of a comprehensive academic counseling program

  • Develop and refine graduation pathways, including traditional, accelerated, credit recovery, dual enrollment, and alternative educational opportunities

  • Support college, career, and postsecondary planning frameworks at the program level

  • Identify gaps in student access to educational opportunities and recommend programmatic solutions

  • Use student data and outcomes to inform counseling program improvements and priorities

Schedule

  • MOHS Academic Counselors are expected to have an average of 40 hours of availability each week on a year-round basis.

  • Availability during school hours, Monday through Friday between 8 am and 4 pm in a U.S. timezone (ET, CT, MT, or PT) is required.

THIS POSITION IS FOR A CURRENT VACANCY, AND THE EMPLOYER INTENDS TO FILL THIS POSITION BY JANUARY 1ST, 2027

Requirements

Requirements

  • Master’s degree in School Counseling, Counseling, or a related field

  • 2 years of experience in a school-based counseling or academic counseling role at the high school level

  • Strong background in academic planning, graduation requirements, and course sequencing

  • Experience supporting students through MTSS intervention, case management, and academic escalation

  • Proven ability to engage students and families in meaningful, solution-focused conversations

  • Experience guiding postsecondary planning, including college, career, and alternative pathways

  • Ability to apply a whole-child academic lens while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries

  • Experience using student data to inform academic decisions and improve counseling practices

  • Comfortable collaborating across teams in a fast-paced, evolving environment

  • Experience in virtual, hybrid, or nontraditional school settings strongly preferred

  • Ability to read and interpret academic transcripts from a wide range of school systems and apply them accurately to MOHS courses and SAP, including in unusual or ambiguous cases

  • Demonstrated ability to manage a full caseload with consistent reliability, meeting deadlines and maintaining accurate, up-to-date records for each student

  • Ability to execute defined processes precisely and completely, including detailed or repetitive administrative tasks (SAP audits, transcript review, etc.)

The ideal candidate brings:

  • Experience with classroom and/or online teaching

  • State certification or licensure as a school counselor (or eligibility)

  • Experience or certification in mental health counseling for schools

  • Experience in other areas of education, such as content creation, assessment design, or assessment administration

  • Experience with caseloads of 200 or more students

Compensation & Benefits

  • The expected starting pay range is $24.95 - $35.07 per hour. Student Advisors at MiaPrep Online High School work an average of 40 hours per week. When working year-round, this can equate to an annual pay range of $51,896 - $72,945.

  • Miaplaza’s compensation philosophy ensures equity and competitiveness while considering the regional differences in living and labor costs. Specific rates will be provided during the hiring process and are aligned with market data and internal equity.

  • Compensation is evaluated twice per year, based on performance.

  • Full-time employees are eligible for health, dental, and vision insurance, inclusive of specialty care options like fertility benefits, mental health services, and chiropractic care, FSA, HSA, and more.

  • All employees are eligible for a 401(k) retirement plan with employer match.

  • PTO is all-purpose time off, and combines traditional vacation and paid sick leave plans into one flexible, inclusive policy. Eligible employees can use PTO for all kinds of absences including: vacation, holidays, illness, injury, family leave, and other personal business. Full-time employees receive 16 hours of floating holiday PTO per quarter and accumulate additional PTO at the rate of 1 hour per every 17 hours worked. Annually, this amounts to approximately 122 hours per year or 15 eight-hour days on average.

  • Parental leave, and other perks and benefits are also available.

  • We invite your family and friends to join our journey! All employees receive free site memberships and discounted MOHS tuition for the children in their household, plus two additional memberships for other children in their lives.

➡️ You canhear our CEO, Johannes Ziegler, discuss our company’s values and future here!

➡️ Learn more by visiting ourcareers page!

Ready to apply?

Join our team at Miaplaza! Start by submitting your application and resume. Our hiring process involves an assessment, followed by two or more interviews and a role-specific assignment.

We're building an inclusive workplace where everyone belongs. As an equal-opportunity employer and E-Verify participant, we welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experiences. We consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, age, or arrest/conviction records in accordance with applicable laws.

Need accommodations during the application process? Simply let us know before your assessment. We'll work with you to provide any necessary adjustments, including alternate versions of the assessment or assignment based on your needs.

​​Looking for Philippines-based candidates

Job Role: Part-Time Bookkeeper

Compensation range: $900 AUD - $1,100 AUD / Monthly

Engagement type:Independent Contractor Agreement

Work Schedule: This role is expected to require roughly 15-20 hours per week. As a contractor, you’ll have flexibility in how you manage your schedule, but availability for occasional collaboration during AU business hours is preferred.

Who We Are: At Hunt St, we help Australian companies hire top remote talent in the Philippines.. You will be hired directly by the client as an independent contractor. We are not an outsourcing agency. All of our roles are 100% remote so you'll be able to work from home.

Who The Client Is: The company is an established surveying and geospatial solutions provider based in Western Australia, specialising in delivering accurate land data and mapping services for a wide range of projects. Using a combination of modern technology, advanced equipment and industry expertise, the team provides solutions across aerial data collection, 3D laser scanning, underground utility detection and conventional land surveying.

Its work supports clients across the property, construction, engineering and infrastructure sectors, partnering with everyone from private property owners and developers to large-scale organisations involved in major civil, road and rail projects. The business is committed to delivering reliable survey information, practical solutions and high-quality results to support projects from initial planning through to completion.

Role Overview: We're looking for an organised, detail-driven Bookkeeper to own the day-to-day finance and admin engine of the business. You'll keep payroll accurate, purchase orders flowing and job information complete, working closely with the survey team in the field and the business owners in the office.

You'll start with a structured handover from the current bookkeeper, with the goal of taking the reins from the start of December.

Key Responsibilities:

Payroll & reconciliations

  • Process payroll accurately and on time in Xero, including timesheets, leave and allowances.
  • Complete payroll reconciliations, matching pay runs, PAYG withholding and superannuation to the ledger.
  • Reconcile bank and credit card accounts regularly, keeping the books clean and current.

Purchase orders & accounts payable

  • Create and send purchase orders to suppliers and subcontractors.
  • Match supplier invoices to POs, code them correctly and prepare payment runs for approval.
  • Keep supplier records organised and follow up on missing invoices or discrepancies.

Job information & surveyor liaison

  • Chase surveyors for job details, hours and supporting information so every job is complete and ready to invoice.
  • Keep job records up to date in WorkflowMax, linking time, costs and POs to the right jobs.
  • Act as a friendly, persistent point of contact between the field team and the office.

Accounts receivable & reporting

  • Raise client invoices from completed job information and track payments.
  • Follow up overdue accounts professionally to support healthy cash flow.
  • Support BAS preparation and month-end processes, and liaise with the external accountant as needed.
  • Prepare simple reports on cash position, outstanding debtors and job status for the owners.

Requirements

  • Experience: 3+ years' bookkeeping experience, ideally with Australian businesses.
  • Systems: Confident in Xero, including payroll. WorkflowMax (or similar job management software) experience is highly regarded.
  • Knowledge: Solid understanding of Australian payroll, superannuation, PAYG and GST.
  • Detail: Meticulous with numbers and records; you catch the small things before they become big things.
  • Communication: Clear, friendly written English and comfortable following up with busy field staff.
  • Ownership: Self-managing and reliable, able to keep tasks moving with minimal supervision.
  • Bonus: Experience in construction, engineering, surveying or other project-based industries.'

What Success looks like:

  • Payroll runs on time and reconciles cleanly every cycle.
  • POs go out promptly and supplier invoices match up first time.
  • Job information is complete, so invoices go out quickly and cash flows steadily.
  • The owners have a clear, current picture of the numbers and more time back in their week.

Work Arrangement & Expectations:

This is a remote role that may be set up as either an independent contractor engagement or via an Employer of Record (EOR), depending on client preferences and legal structure.

To ensure alignment and transparency, successful candidates will be expected to:

  • Be available for meetings and collaboration during core [AEST or PHT] business hours
  • Disclose any existing ongoing roles or client work
  • Reflect this engagement on their LinkedIn profile (clearly marked as “Independent Contractor” if not employed via EOR)

jobs.excerpt: The Patient Journey Director CEERJ enables journey from first symptom to diagnosis, referral and appropriate care outcomes faster, clearer and fairer for people living with C3G/IC-MPGN and severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG) across CEERJ.
jobs.description:
The Patient Journey Director CEERJ enables journey from first symptom to diagnosis, referral and appropriate care outcomes faster, clearer and fairer for people living with C3G/IC-MPGN and severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG) across CEERJ.

The role is driven by a genuine passion for improving the patient journey. It identifies where patients are delayed, missed or lost, partners with country medical and commercial teams to understand why, and turns those barriers into practical, compliant and measurable initiatives. This includes leading the integration of medical devices and diagnostic-enabling platforms (Florio, Enfuse, diagnostics) into patient journey frameworks for strategic CEERJ therapeutic areas (C3G/IC-MPGN, sHTG and secondarily haemophilia).

The role operates in a fast-moving, changing environment. The holder works in an agile way: sets few clear priorities, adapts quickly as launches, access and evidence evolve, and turns insight into executive-ready plans that are communicated clearly to the Brand Teams, Leadership Teams and Core Medical Team.

Main responsibilities:

Own the patient journey agenda for C3G/IC-MPGN and sHTG across CEERJ. Define, maintain and continuously refine a regional patient journey framework that identifies diagnostic difficulties, delays and post-therapy difficulties, and translates them into prioritized, measurable initiatives.

Partner with countries to map and clear barriers & opportunities. Work alongside country leaders and field teams to map country-specific barriers (awareness, testing access, laboratory and biopsy pathways, referral fragmentation, expert centre availability, non-pharmaceutical therapy optimization opportunities)

Build & resource executive plans. Develop concise, prioritized patient journey improvement projects with clear milestones, owners, dependencies and KPIs. Resource and adjust them rapidly as conditions change. Report progress to senior leadership in Core Medical Team, CEERJ LT and Brand Team forums.

Lead projects and matrix teams: drive relevant Patient Journey projects and allocated matrix teams from kick off to close out ensuring clear planning, budgeting, delivery and reporting on time and within budget

Lead integration of medical devices and enabling platforms. Lead integration of Florio, Enfuse, diagnostics and pipeline tools into patient journey frameworks across CEERJ. Ensure stakeholder value, country readiness and compliant use. Track adoption, escalate barriers and propose solutions.

Generate and act on patient journey insights. Interact with external community to enable systematic collection and synthesis of insights from HCPs, KOLs, diagnostic initiatives, patient organisations and country teams. Turn them into clear recommendations that change plans and decisions.

Sobi’s share is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. More about Sobi at sobi.com and LinkedIn.

Sobi Culture

At Sobi, we refuse to accept the status quo. This is because we have witnessed first-hand the challenges facing those affected by rare diseases and have used this knowledge to shape our business to find new ways of helping them.
As a specialized biopharmaceutical company, we are dedicated to rare diseases. And we see this focus as a strength. By effectively turning our research into ground-breaking treatments, we help make medicine more accessible and open more possibilities for patients and more opportunities for those caring for them. This has been our approach since day one, but we know we can’t change the world of rare diseases on our own. Accomplishing this requires strong partnerships with patients, partners and stakeholders across the entire value chain. Together, we define how our business can create solutions that serve the needs of those affected by rare diseases while facilitating sustainable growth.

At Sobi, each person brings their unique talents to work as a team and make a difference. We are dedicated to developing and delivering innovative therapies to improve the lives of rare disease patients and our edge comes from our team of people.

jobs.description:
If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.

Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)

This is a Stanford Health Care job.

A Brief Overview
Requires review of medical record documentation to accurately assign International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10-CM/PCS), as well as assignment of the Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) / All Patient Refined - Diagnosis Related Group (APR-DRG) and abstracts specific data elements for each account in compliance with federal and state regulations. This position codes the majority of patient types of inpatient records, including more complex cases such as Intensive Care. Follows the Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting, the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA) Standards of Ethical Coding, as well as all American Hospital Association (AHA) Coding Clinic guidance. Follows Stanford Health Care policies and procedures and maintains required quality and productivity standards. Reviews, abstracts and assigns accurate and ethical ICD-10-CM/PCS codes to inpatient services. Ensures compliance with third party, State and Federal regulations. Reviews, analyzes and abstracts physician/other documentation for diagnoses, procedures, and other services provided. Obtains missing information and/or clarifies existing information. Completes volume of work from work queues per departmental productivity standards. Groups codes and completed product into payment group. Analyzes information for optimal and approprite reimbursement. Ensures compliance with all appropriate coding, billing and data collection regulations and procedures. Uses appropriate software to validate information. Utilizes Epic, 3M Coding and Reimbursement System (Encoder), 3M CDIS, 3M Audit Expert, MS Office, and other software as appropriate to compile and validate medical information.

Locations

Stanford Health Care

What you will do

  • Reviews medical record documentation and accurately assigns appropriate ICD-10 diagnosis and procedure codes, leading to the assignment of the correct Medicare Severity-Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) or All Patient Refined Diagnosis Related Group (APR-DRG). The Inpatient Coding Specialist II is responsible for verification of the patient's discharge disposition, assignment of the correct sources of admission for state regulation reporting purposes, and ensuring the appropriate present on admission (POA) indicators are assigned to each code. The assigned codes must support the reason for the visit that is documented by the provider in order to support the care provided.
  • Correctly abstracts required data per facility specifications.
  • Responsible for monitoring Discharged Not Billed accounts, and as a team, ensuring timely, compliant processing of inpatient accounts through the revenue cycle.
  • Collaborates with Clinical Documentation Specialists (CDSs) and members of the medical staff to ensure completeness of documentation in the medical records so that appropriate codes, and, ultimately, the correct Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) may be assigned.
  • Responsible for ensuring accuracy and maintaining established quality and productivity standards.
  • Demonstrates a high degree of independence in performance of responsibilities, working effectively without direct supervision. Exhibits strong time management, problem solving and communication skills.
  • Possesses critical thinking, good judgment and decision making skills.
  • Demonstrates excellent written and oral communication skills.
  • Remains abreast of current Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) requirements as well as Correct Coding Initiative (CCI) edits, Hospital Acquired Conditions (HACs), Patient Safety Indicators (PSIs), and when applicable, National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs,) including the addition of appropriate modifiers to ensure a clean claim the first time through.
  • Maintains competency and accuracy while utilizing tools of the trade such as the 3M encoder, 3M Audit Expert process (3M AES), 3M Clinical Documentation Improvement System (3M CDIS) and abstracting systems, as well as all reference materials.
  • Follows all established Stanford Health Care policies and procedures.
  • Attends required system, hospital and departmental meetings and educational sessions as established by leadership, as well as completion of required annual learning programs, to ensure continued education and growth.

Education Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or GED equivalent

Experience Qualifications

  • Five (5) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience

Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Successful completion of the Coder Proficiency Exam (pre-hire)
  • Ability to adapt to and deal with change and ambiguity
  • Ability to plan, organize, prioritize, work independently and meet deadlines
  • Ability to comply with the American Health Information Management Association’s Code of Ethics and Standards and apply Uniform Hospital Discharge Data Set (UHDDS) standards
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships
  • Ability to manage, organize, prioritize, multi-task and adapt to changing priorities
  • Ability to solve technical and non-technical problems
  • Ability to utilize the ICD-10-CM/PCS and CPT-4 coding conventions to code medical record entries; abstract information from medical records; read medical record documentation; assign accurate codes for grouping of MS-DRGs and APR-DRGs
  • Ability to work effectively through and with others
  • Knowledge of diagnosis/procedure DRG grouping schemes such as MS-DRGs and APR-DRGs
  • Knowledge of health information systems for computer application to medical records
  • Ability to foster effective working relationships and build consensus
  • Ability to work effectively with individuals at all levels of the organization
  • Knowledge of CCI (Correct Coding Initiatives) and CMS compliance issues
  • Knowledge of computer systems and software used in functional area

Licenses and Certifications

  • RHIT - Registered Health Information Technician or

The position leads the post-certification experience, develops differentiated value propositions, and mobilizes collaboration and collective action initiatives among companies and ecosystem partners. Its leadership must strengthen participation, satisfaction (NPS), retention, and commitment to recertification through management of the regional team.

jobs.description:
Chief of Staff (Integrator)

Part-time (0.5 FTE, about 20 hours per week) | Remote | Reports to: Chief Executive Officer

About UNDIVIDED

UNDIVIDED is a Christian faith-based organization committed to building meaningful impact through community-centered work, relationship-driven engagement, cultivating spaces of belonging, and moving people into redemptive action for healing and justice in their communities. How we work together is shaped by the UNDIVIDED Way: Open Hands, Linked Arms, Hopeful Hearts, and Bold Steps.

Position Summary

The Chief of Staff turns the CEO's vision into an operating rhythm the organization can count on. In the Visionary and Integrator model, the CEO sets direction and the Chief of Staff makes it happen: running the Executive Leadership Team (ELT), holding shared services to a clear standard, and developing leaders.

This is a part-time, remote role, so it is built around a small number of priorities fully kept rather than everything at once. The Chief of Staff does not run the shared-service functions day to day. The Operations Director and team deliver them; the Chief of Staff sets standards, removes blockers and holds accountability.

The ideal candidate is a systems thinker and people developer who brings order to complexity, builds trust across teams, and leads in a way that makes UNDIVIDED's Postures visible.

Role at a Glance

  • Reports to: CEO
  • Direct report: Operations Director
  • Works with (no reporting line): ELT members, who report to the CEO and are accountable to the Chief of Staff for ELT commitments, priorities and follow-through
  • Time allocation (guide): ELT leadership and Integrator work about 40% · Shared services oversight about 35% · Coaching and leader development about 25%
  • Decides: ELT meeting agendas and cadence; tracking of priorities and KPIs; shared-service standards and process changes; Operations Director goals and performance
  • Recommends to the CEO: Annual priorities and budget; changes to roles, structure or headcount; policy changes; spending above the CEO-approved limit
  • Escalates: Legal and compliance risk (to counsel, with the CEO); complaints of harassment, discrimination or policy violations (to HR or the Board-designated channel)

What this role is not. It is not the HR complaint channel, legal counsel or the day-to-day payroll or finance processor. When a conflict involves a complaint or possible policy violation, the Chief of Staff routes it to HR or the Board-designated channel rather than resolving it informally.

Key Responsibilities

1. Lead the Executive Team as Integrator (about 40%)

  • Translate the CEO's vision into a small set of quarterly priorities, each with one owner, a measure and a due date.
  • Run ELT meetings: set agendas, facilitate decisions, keep a decision log and follow up on commitments.
  • Maintain the organizational KPI scorecard, review it with the ELT, and recommend changes in priorities based on the data.
  • Align initiatives across teams and surface dependencies and capacity limits before they become conflicts.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO, and make sure staff understand ELT decisions and have a way to share their perspective.

2. Hold shared services to a clear standard (about 35%)

The Operations Director and team deliver these services. The Chief of Staff sets standards, removes blockers and holds accountability.

  • People: oversee onboarding, training and development, and the performance cycle, partnering with HR on people policies and employee relations.
  • Operational systems and IT: set expectations for data management, systems and measuring organizational outcomes.
  • Finance and payroll: oversee the budget process, monthly financial reporting and payroll accuracy, and recommend budget decisions to the CEO.
  • Legal and compliance: coordinate with outside counsel, keep a compliance calendar, and flag risk in key decisions to the CEO.

Open Hands

Hopeful Hearts

Bold Steps

Success Profile

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Search & Personalization
jobs.excerpt: About Bask HealthBask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Search & Personalization to design, build, and improve intelligent search, discovery, and personalization capabilities across Bask Health's platform.

This is a hands-on engineering role focused on making information easier to find, experiences more relevant, and complex workflows more intuitive. You'll work with machine learning models, information retrieval systems, embeddings, ranking algorithms, and production application infrastructure to build search and recommendation experiences that deliver measurable value.

Bask Health supports multiple interconnected applications, including merchant-facing tools, patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce systems. You'll help develop the underlying intelligence that allows these applications to surface useful information, prioritize relevant results, and adapt experiences to different user needs.

Your work may include semantic search, hybrid retrieval, intelligent ranking, contextual recommendations, personalized content discovery, and retrieval services that support AI-powered applications.

You'll be responsible for more than model experimentation. You'll design and deploy production systems, develop data pipelines, establish evaluation methods, monitor performance, and improve search relevance through ongoing testing and iteration.

You'll collaborate closely with product managers, backend engineers, frontend engineers, and applied AI teams to understand how users interact with the platform and where better discovery or personalization can reduce friction.

Because Bask operates in healthcare-related environments, you'll also need to consider privacy, access controls, and the limitations of personalized recommendations. Systems that influence sensitive healthcare workflows must follow approved product and clinical boundaries rather than independently making medical decisions.

We're looking for someone who combines strong machine learning fundamentals with practical software engineering skills and enjoys building intelligent systems that people use every day.

What You'll Do

  • Design, build, and deploy machine learning systems for search, discovery, ranking, and personalization.
  • Develop semantic search capabilities that improve how users find information across Bask Health's applications.
  • Build and optimize retrieval pipelines using embeddings, vector search, and traditional search methods.
  • Design hybrid search systems combining lexical matching, semantic retrieval, and relevance ranking.
  • Develop ranking models and algorithms that prioritize useful search results.
  • Build recommendation systems that surface relevant platform features, resources, or workflow information.
  • Develop contextual personalization capabilities based on approved user and application signals.
  • Work with product teams to identify opportunities to improve search relevance and information discovery.
  • Build scalable indexing, retrieval, and search-serving infrastructure.
  • Design data pipelines that support search models, ranking systems, and recommendation features.
  • Develop approaches for generating, storing, updating, and evaluating embeddings.
  • Experiment with learning-to-rank methods and machine learning-based relevance improvements.
  • Implement query understanding, query expansion, and search intent interpretation where appropriate.
  • Improve search performance across structured and unstructured data sources.
  • Collaborate with applied AI engineers to support retrieval-augmented generation applications.
  • Develop retrieval services that can be reused across patient, merchant, and operational applications.
  • Define and track search quality metrics, including relevance, recall, precision, and ranking performance.
  • Design offline evaluation datasets and benchmarking procedures for search and recommendation systems.
  • Collaborate with product teams to conduct controlled experiments and measure user experience improvements.
  • Optimize search latency, throughput, infrastructure utilization, and operational costs.
  • Implement monitoring and observability for production search and personalization services.
  • Investigate search quality issues, indexing failures, and ranking inconsistencies.
  • Ensure retrieval and personalization systems respect user permissions and data access boundaries.
  • Design appropriate safeguards for sensitive healthcare-related recommendations.
  • Work with backend and frontend engineers to integrate search and recommendation features into production applications.
  • Contribute to architecture decisions involving search infrastructure, databases, and machine learning services.
  • Mentor engineers and share expertise in information retrieval, ranking, and production ML engineering.
  • Own search and personalization initiatives from technical design through deployment, measurement, and ongoing improvement.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional experience in machine learning engineering, software engineering, search engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience building and deploying machine learning systems in production.
  • Strong programming skills in Python and experience developing production software services.
  • Experience building search, recommendation, ranking, or information retrieval systems.
  • Strong understanding of machine learning fundamentals and applied statistical methods.
  • Familiarity with modern information retrieval techniques and search relevance optimization.
  • Experience with embeddings, vector representations, or semantic similarity methods.
  • Understanding of lexical search, semantic search, and hybrid retrieval approaches.
  • Experience designing or integrating scalable search infrastructure.
  • Strong understanding of ranking algorithms and relevance evaluation.
  • Experience working with structured and unstructured datasets.
  • Familiarity with data processing, feature engineering, and machine learning pipelines.
  • Experience building backend APIs and integrating machine learning services into applications.
  • Understanding of database design, indexing, and query performance.
  • Experience evaluating model or search system performance using quantitative metrics.
  • Familiarity with offline evaluation, experimentation, and performance benchmarking.
  • Experience optimizing production systems for latency, scalability, and reliability.
  • Understanding of cloud infrastructure and deployment practices.
  • Familiarity with monitoring, logging, and troubleshooting production services.
  • Strong software engineering practices, including testing, code review, and version control.
  • Understanding of data privacy, access controls, and secure application design.
  • Ability to translate product requirements into practical machine learning solutions.
  • Experience collaborating with product managers and cross-functional engineering teams.
  • Ability to independently own complex engineering projects from design through deployment.
  • Strong analytical thinking, communication skills, and technical problem-solving abilities.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building personalized recommendation systems for SaaS or consumer applications.
  • Familiarity with learning-to-rank models and neural ranking approaches.
  • Experience with approximate nearest neighbor search and vector indexing techniques.
  • Familiarity with Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Vespa, or comparable search infrastructure.
  • Experience using vector databases such as Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, or pgvector.
  • Experience with embedding models and transformer-based retrieval systems.
  • Familiarity with cross-encoders, reranking models, and multi-stage retrieval pipelines.
  • Experience developing query understanding or natural language search features.
  • Experience building retrieval systems for large language model applications.
  • Familiarity with retrieval-augmented generation architectures.
  • Experience with recommendation approaches such as collaborative filtering or content-based ranking.
  • Experience with online experimentation, A/B testing, and search relevance measurement.
  • Familiarity with clickstream analysis and user behavior modeling.
  • Experience developing real-time or near-real-time personalization systems.
  • Experience with large-scale data processing frameworks or distributed computing.
  • Familiarity with AWS and cloud-based machine learning infrastructure.
  • Experience building search or recommendation features for e-commerce platforms.
  • Experience with healthcare, telehealth, or other privacy-sensitive software.
  • Understanding of HIPAA and healthcare data privacy considerations.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor or Claude Code.

Gestionnaire des comptes fournisseurs Résumé du poste Le ou la gestionnaire des comptes fournisseurs est responsable de diriger la fonction des comptes fournisseurs, en veillant à l’efficacité et à l’exactitude du traitement des factures, des paiements aux fournisseurs, de la conformité, de la production de rapports et de l’amélioration continue des processus. La personne retenue combinera une solide expertise en comptes fournisseurs avec une passion pour l’amélioration des processus, l’analyse de données, les outils alimentés par l’intelligence artificielle et le leadership d’équipe. Principales responsabilités

Diriger, encadrer et développer une équipe performante de comptes fournisseurs. Superviser les opérations quotidiennes des comptes fournisseurs afin d’assurer le traitement rapide et exact des factures et des paiements. Piloter les initiatives d’amélioration des processus, d’automatisation et d’adoption de l’intelligence artificielle au sein de la fonction des comptes fournisseurs. Élaborer et maintenir les rapports, tableaux de bord et indicateurs de performance des comptes fournisseurs. Gérer les relations avec les fournisseurs et résoudre les problèmes de paiement nécessitant une intervention de niveau supérieur. Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes des approvisionnements, de la trésorerie, des finances, des opérations et les autres parties prenantes de l’entreprise. Veiller au respect des politiques de l’entreprise, des contrôles internes et des exigences d’audit. Soutenir les activités de clôture mensuelle et annuelle. Contribuer aux initiatives d’amélioration du fonds de roulement et des flux de trésorerie. Identifier les possibilités d’améliorer l’efficacité, l’évolutivité et les niveaux de service de l’ensemble du processus des comptes fournisseurs.

Baccalauréat en comptabilité, en finance, en administration des affaires ou dans un domaine connexe. Expérience avec les systèmes ERP et les plateformes d’automatisation des comptes fournisseurs. Maîtrise avancée d’Excel et expérience avec les outils de production de rapports et d’analyse de données. Expérience dans l’utilisation d’outils d’intelligence artificielle tels que Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT ou des technologies similaires afin d’améliorer la productivité et la prise de décision. Succès démontré dans la direction d’initiatives d’amélioration des processus et de gestion du changement.

Un leader solide qui développe et motive les équipes. Patiente, professionnelle et orientée vers les solutions. Analytique et axé(e) sur les données, avec des compétences avancées en Excel et en production de rapports. À l’aise avec les systèmes ERP, les outils d’automatisation et les technologies émergentes en intelligence artificielle. Axé(e) sur l’amélioration continue, l’innovation et l’excellence opérationnelle. Capable de réussir dans un environnement dynamique et multisites tout en gérant efficacement des priorités concurrentes.

About TachyonShift

TachyonShift builds, runs and governs AI and cloud systems for customers. We started as a managed cloud practice. Customers asked for AI in production, the missing piece was governance, and we built UnifAI, an enterprise AI platform with governed agents, every major model and one audit trail. Today one team builds the system, operates it after launch and stays accountable for the result. Every engagement has a named senior engineer, written success metrics and a working demo in front of the customer every week.

The role

Build things that run in production. Lead the work that puts a governed, working AI system in front of a customer in weeks.

A forward deployed engineer works inside the customer's business. You sit with the people who do the work, learn the process and the data, and build the system that replaces the manual steps. As a senior engineer you are the named engineer on the engagement: the customer's technical point of contact, the person who writes the plan, leads the build, and answers for the result after launch.

What you will do

  • Work backwards with the customer: write the announcement, the success metrics, and the hard questions before the first line of code
  • Design and build production AI systems on the customer's real data: retrieval, multi-step agents, workflow automation, integrations, and the code that makes them dependable
  • Choose the right model for each step, from any provider, and keep the system model-neutral so a model swap is a configuration change
  • Write evaluation tests before launch and design the human verification and audit trail for every output where an error costs money
  • Demo working software to the customer every week and change course on what you learn
  • Operate what you ship under the operating agreement: monitoring, incident response, runbooks, and a monthly results review
  • Mentor engineers and set the technical bar on your engagement

What success looks like in your first 90 days

  • Lead an engagement from working-backwards document to a working version on real data, demoed weekly
  • Ship evaluation tests and a monitoring plan with the first release
  • Leave runbooks that let another engineer or the customer operate the system
  • Raise one improvement to how the team scopes, builds, or verifies AI systems

What you bring

  • Eight or more years building and running production software, including hands-on delivery of LLM-based systems
  • Strong Python or TypeScript, and sound judgment on data models, APIs, and cloud architecture
  • Experience integrating with enterprise systems such as CRM, ERP, ticketing, identity, or a data warehouse
  • Comfort working directly with customer teams, executives included, and saying plainly what will and will not work
  • A record of owning a system after launch, not only building it
  • The habit of telling the customer what you know, what you do not know, and what it will cost

Helpful, not required

  • Experience with agent frameworks, fine-tuning, or evaluation tooling
  • Work in finance, professional services, or the public sector, where audit requirements are real
  • Experience with AWS, Azure, or GCP at the platform level

How we work together

  • Customer Value First: we measure success by the customer's outcome, not by features shipped.
  • Full Ownership Mindset: we own problems end to end and fix what needs fixing, whoever's job it is.
  • Results Drive Recognition: we recognize contribution, capability and results.
  • Integrity: we do the right thing even when nobody is looking.
  • Respect for Every Person: we treat everyone with dignity and listen first, whether they are a customer, a colleague or a candidate.

Working here

Remote across the United States. Small teams led by senior people, on customers' real data and systems. You see what your work does.

How we hire

We hire on demonstrated ability. Apply on this page and tell us about work you are proud of, such as a system you built, a problem you solved or a decision you owned. Expect a short screen, a conversation with a senior member of the team, a review of work you have done, and a final conversation. Apply on this page only. We never ask for payment, bank details or government ID during hiring.

Equal Opportunity

Role summary
The Practice Director, SDLC leads the development and evolution of Valiantys’ North American Software Development Life Cycle practice. The role helps clients modernize and orchestrate the full flow of delivering and operating software—from discovery and planning through design, implementation, testing, deployment and ongoing maintenance. It combines practice leadership, delivery excellence, commercial leadership and solution ownership. A consultative mindset is essential: uncovering business and industry context, shaping options into practical roadmaps, and connecting technical choices to measurable outcomes. The role is focused on North American execution and operates in a global matrix, aligning regional priorities with the direction set by the Global Head of Practice.
Responsibilities
Practice leadership
• Act as the Global Head of Practice’s regional delegate, representing Valiantys in strategic client, partner and Atlassian interactions and embedding the global SDLC strategy in North America.
• Build the regional practice around end-to-end software delivery transformation, spanning engineering workflows, DevOps practices, governance, quality, delivery speed and measurable business outcomes.
• Serve as the regional SDLC solution authority, combining strong Atlassian platform knowledge with a broad view of complementary engineering and DevOps technologies, and mobilizing deep specialist expertise where needed.
• Maintain a current view of established and emerging engineering and DevOps technologies and leading practices, including Atlassian products (Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Jira Service Management and Rovo), complementary tools such as Xray and SonarQube, and DX and similar capabilities for engineering metrics and insights. Assess how these capabilities align and integrate with Atlassian and client environments, including evolving AI capabilities.
• Keep the practice skills matrix, capability plans and enablement priorities current across SDLC transformation, platforms, delivery and AI-enabled ways of working.
• Foster a collaborative, high-performance practice culture that shares field insight, leading practices and lessons learned to improve client value and Valiantys revenue.
• Ensure approved practice and company methods, governance and tools are applied consistently across North America.
• Own the regional SDLC Practice shadow P&L, including investment in solution-component development and practice enablement. Partner with the Global Head of Practice and Head of Delivery to clarify regional versus global ownership of training, certification, enablement and solution-development investments, and surface gaps where ownership is not defined.
Delivery
• Define and oversee delivery approaches for complex or high-impact SDLC transformation engagements, ensuring alignment with client outcomes, technical feasibility, operating-model needs, Valiantys standards and leading practices.
• Lead consultative discovery with client executives and delivery teams, translating ambiguous business needs into target operating models, SDLC roadmaps, solution architectures and phased plans with measurable outcomes.
• Bring expertise in one or more client domains, particularly complex or regulated environments, and adapt SDLC transformation to industry-specific business models and constraints, including security, compliance and adoption needs.
• Act as a senior advisor to strategic clients, helping leaders connect investment in engineering and DevOps improvement to measurable business outcomes.
• Provide design assurance across the full software delivery lifecycle, including discovery, planning, feasibility, system design, implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance, with attention to security, compliance, resilience, observability, scalability, operational readiness and cost effectiveness.
• Oversee key deliverables and delivery risks where appropriate, including adoption, governance, quality and operating-model considerations that extend beyond a tooling implementation. Assess the delivery, support and maintenance implications of AI-enabled solutions, including clear ownership and appropriate lifecycle plans.
• Guide client onboarding, enablement and iterative improvement so transformed SDLC capabilities are adopted across technical teams and deliver their intended business value.
• Support the Delivery Management team in forecasting the skills and capacity required for the regional practice.
• Partner with practice and delivery leadership on plans for training, certifications, internal enablement and solution development, in line with the agreed practice investment model.
Sales support
• Support sales on complex or large-scale SDLC opportunities, providing credible executive and technical leadership while ensuring feasibility and alignment with practice strategy.
• Run regular pipeline reviews and deal clinics to identify where repeatable offerings should be used and where a tailored solution is justified.
• Guide sales teams on the value, scope and appropriate use of the SDLC solution catalogue, including AI-enabled capabilities where they provide an evidenced client benefit.
• Contribute to the validation of statements of work, estimates and delivery models to support accurate scoping, commercial discipline and delivery feasibility.
• Work with Marketing, Alliances and the Transformation practice (Tx) on SDLC go-to-market strategy, thought leadership, case studies and market messages.
Product and solution ownership
• Collaborate with the Head of Solutions and Global Head of Practice to manage the lifecycle of SDLC solutions, accelerators and training offers from idea through retirement.
• Lead regional development of repeatable solution components for the full delivery-project lifecycle, including discovery materials, repeatable roadmaps and delivery-ready project assets and deliverables.
• Develop repeatable SDLC transformation components, including AI-enabled patterns that strengthen planning, knowledge flow, engineering productivity, quality, service operations or governance; account for their design, delivery, support and maintenance implications.
• Act as design authority for repeatable solution components, ensuring they support product marketing, delivery quality, sales efficiency and measurable client outcomes.
• Enable Practice consultants, sales and delivery teams to use approved components effectively and consistently.
• Own the regional IP development lifecycle, ensuring investments align with the strategic direction of the practice and can be scaled or reused.
• Ensure delivery lessons and client evidence inform continuous improvement of offerings, methods and enablement.
• Coordinate with other practices to remove duplication and close gaps across Valiantys’ solution portfolio.
Your team and partners
• Head of Delivery, North America — line manager
• Global Head of Practice — dotted-line manager
• Principal Consultants and other Practice team members, where applicable
• Product Owners and Head of Solutions
• Delivery Management team
• Sales, Marketing and Alliances teams, including the Transformation practice (Tx)
• People and Culture team
• Global Partner Manager and strategic partners

About TCP Software

For more than 30 years, TCP has helped organizations engage their people by providing flexible, mobile timekeeping and workforce management solutions. Trusted by tens of thousands of customers and millions of users, TCP delivers best-in-class technology and personalized support to organizations of all sizes in the public and private sectors to meet their complex timekeeping, employee scheduling, leave management, and other workforce needs. Growth is happening, and our vision for a successful future is clear — we'd love for you to join us on this journey!

For more information on TCP Software, visit www.tcpsoftware.com or follow us on LinkedIn or Facebook.

About the Role

The Senior Product Marketing Manager for Humanity Schedule will serve as the strategic marketing lead for TCP’s dynamic employee scheduling solution. You will develop a deep understanding of our customers, buyers, market, and competitive landscape and translate those insights into clear positioning, differentiated messaging, effective go-to-market strategies, and compelling sales enablement.

This is a highly cross-functional role that sits at the intersection of Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing. You will influence product strategy, lead major launches, strengthen our market position, and help our commercial teams communicate the business value of Humanity Schedule. The ideal candidate is both strategic and hands-on, comfortable shaping the narrative, creating the tools, and driving the execution required to accelerate pipeline, win competitive opportunities, and increase customer adoption.

What You’ll Be Doing

As a Senior Product Marketing Manager for our Humanity Schedule product, you'll be responsible for:

  • Market Intelligence – Become an expert on our buyers, who they are, and how they buy our software. You’ll build an understanding of the buyer journey and its relationship to our sales process to help the company make intelligent, market/buyer-centric decisions.
  • Product Messaging – Work together with product management to construct messages that clearly articulate the value our Humanity Schedule provides, the challenges it solves, and why customers should deploy our solution now.
  • Content Creation – Work collaboratively with our content team to develop content for sales and partner enablement, partner engagements, and external marketing/demand generation campaigns and communications.
  • GTM Strategy – Assist in executing our GTM strategy, including identification of target market/customer, buyer persona interviews, core use cases, and the customer journey.
  • Sales and Partner Enablement - Establish competitive battlecards and work closely with Sales and Partner Enablement to conduct trainings that ensure internal and extended sales forces are fully educated on product features and new releases. Help conduct win/loss analysis on a quarterly basis.
  • Product Packaging – Work across multiple departments, including marketing, finance, operations, product management, and sales to define product structure, including naming, packaging, licensing, and pricing to simplify the sales/acquisition process and encourage customer adoption.
  • Product Launch & Excitement - Own and coordinate product launches to maximize awareness. Drive product excitement into key segments to maximize adoption and usage.
  • Campaign Planning & Execution – Work with senior marketing leaders to craft program plans and define inbound and outbound marketing channels. Work with Demand Gen to define and build email nurture/drip programs and relevant target segments across owned and paid media.
  • Measurement and Analytics – Work with marketing operations, product marketing, and marketing leadership to define campaign targets and build reports and dashboards to report on program performance and ROI.
  • Competitive Intelligence - Study and monitor the key players in our industry (i.e., potential alternatives to our product), help define how we are different, and why our differentiators are important to our target audience.
  • Spokesperson – Serve as a primary company spokesperson and advocate for Humanity Schedule while engaging with analysts, press, customers, and investors.

How You’ll be Measured

Success in this role will be measured by your ability to:

  • Strengthen market positioning – Establish clear, differentiated positioning and messaging across priority markets, industries, and buyer personas.
  • Deliver effective launches – Lead coordinated launches that drive awareness, sales readiness, pipeline, and customer adoption.
  • Improve commercial performance – Equip Sales and partners with the training, competitive intelligence, and content needed to improve buyer engagement and win rates.
  • Generate actionable insight – Build a strong understanding of buyer needs, market trends, the customer journey, and competitive dynamics.
  • Influence strategy – Translate market insights into recommendations for product priorities, packaging, pricing, segmentation, and go-to-market.
  • Drive measurable impact – Demonstrate contribution to pipeline, revenue, adoption, and retention.
  • Build cross-functional alignment – Create clarity, accountability, and momentum across Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (preferred)
  • 5-7 years of experience in product marketing; preferably at least 1-2 years in a senior position
  • An understanding of and experience in the B2B/SaaS technology – previous experience with time-tracking, scheduling, or workforce management solutions is a bonus but not a requirement
  • Familiarity with frontline employee scheduling in the healthcare, retail & hospitality, construction, and/or manufacturing industries is preferred, but not required
  • Ability to write about technology clearly with the ability to distill complex business and technology concepts into easily understood value statements.
  • Adaptive personality, highly organized and self-motivated, takes ownership and delivering results in a fast-paced environment - should be comfortable with high ambiguity.
  • Ability to understand technology at its core functions and articulate the benefits of the technology at a business level.
  • Demonstrated success in analyzing market opportunities, defining market requirements, and managing go-to-market for software and service products in a B2B environment.
  • Quantitative, creative, and exceptional communications skills

Company Description

Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart, we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap, built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate, the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here.

Your role

Microsoft 365 is where work happens. It keeps getting bigger, busier and harder to keep under control. ShareGate helps more than 100,000 IT pros move, understand and govern their Microsoft 365 environments with confidence. AI now lets us build faster than ever, so the real question is whether we're building the right things. We're looking for a Software Development Manager to bridge the two: someone who moves fast with every tool available and keeps the team focused on what makes a difference for customers.

Your impact:

  • Drive customer value by making sure what the team ships improves the customer experience, and challenge work that doesn't.
  • Use AI to build faster, raise the quality of what we deliver and simplify maintenance, while keeping every squad focused on the right priorities.
  • Build squads that fully own their part of the product, from design to production.
  • Keep the roadmap ahead of the team by working with Product and Design, so delivery speed turns into customer value.
  • Raise the bar on engineering practices and on the people behind them, from coaching to hiring developers who make the team stronger.

Your team

AI is changing how we build software. Our developers already use agents to design, build, test and maintain the product, and we ship faster than ever. The next challenge isn't going faster. It's making sure that speed turns into more value for customers: better experiences, sharper insights and problems solved before they become problems. Under the hood, a data ingestion platform continuously reads Microsoft 365 environments so customers always see what's really going on.

You'll lead 12 developers organized in 3 squads, each owning its part of the product. We work closely with Product and Design, decide fast and fix course even faster. We're remote-first, with access to our Montreal office.

What you'll bring

  • Experience managing a software team of 5+ developers, from hiring to coaching, with the managerial courage to have the hard performance conversations, give direct feedback and keep standards high so the people around you grow;
  • A strong product mindset: you start from the customer problem and you're comfortable saying no to work that doesn't solve it;
  • Solid knowledge of modern software development practices and architecture, enough to challenge technical decisions;
  • A track record of improving how a team works with AI and automation, and measuring the impact;
  • Comfort with ambiguity and with making fast, reversible decisions.

Most of this sounds like you? Apply.

What the job comes with

  • Base salary: $155 000 to $185 000.This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale.Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions.
  • Annual bonus program.
  • LTIP program, share in Workleap's long-term growth.
  • RRSP + Family health insurance + telemedicine + annual wellness budget.
  • Flexible vacation policy.
  • Remote work, with access to our Montreal office.
  • In-person gatherings twice a year.
  • Claude access, for everyone.

What drives us

At Workleap, we build software that sits at the center of how people experience work, every day, at every level.

We move fast. Priorities shift, decisions get made with the information we have, and we iterate. If you thrive on intensity and ambiguity doesn't slow you down, you'll feel right at home.
We're builders. We do what it takes to move forward. AI is part of our toolkit. We use it to go faster and decide smarter, not to replace judgment.

If you want real impact and a place where your decisions matter, this is it.

How we hire

Transparency is how we hire — for you as much as for us.

Here's how it works: a first call with a recruiter, then a virtual interview with the hiring manager. You'll then complete a take-home case study, followed by a meet with future colleagues to discuss it together. Depending on the role, the process may vary slightly — your recruiter will walk you through it on your first call.

We use AI to support certain steps of the process, but every hiring decision remains human.

We can't wait to meet you.

By applying, you confirm that you have read and agree to our privacy policy.

Job summary

The Event Operations Specialist - Registration is our Cvent specialist for external events and campaigns. You own the Cvent registration experience from start to finish: building registration sites, managing invitations and attendee data, supporting check-in at live events when necessary, setting up registration for events run by other team members, and making sure every, campaign, registration, and attendance record flows cleanly (and accurately) into Salesforce. You also manage your own portfolio of virtual events, and you act as the department’s project manager, keeping work organized and helping streamline how the team operates. You work closely with the email marketing team, the content team (copywriters, designers, and others), local offices, and event specialists to make registering for a Mercer Advisors event convenient, polished, and on brand.

Essential job functions

Cvent registration site build and administration

  • Build and launch Cvent registration websites, forms, and confirmation pages for in-person, virtual, and hybrid events, using reusable templates that reflect Mercer Advisors branding.
  • Partner with the content team (copywriters, designers, and others) on registration site copy, imagery, branding, and request, review, and approve assets so every site is polished and on brand.
  • Partner with the email marketing team to align registration sites with invitation, reminder, and follow-up emails, coordinating timing, messaging, links, and registration tracking before each send.
  • Configure Cvent registration paths with conditional logic, multiple attendee types (such as clients, prospects, guests, and team members), capacity limits, waitlists, and approval workflows.
  • Test every Cvent registration site end to end before launch, proofing content, logic, confirmation emails, and reporting for accuracy.
  • Serve as the Cvent power user for local events, maintaining account standards, templates, user access, and data integrity, and documenting the build process so others can follow it.
  • Confirm registration pages and communications meet accessibility, privacy, and compliance requirements.

Attendee management and communications

  • Manage the attendee experience from invitation through post-event follow-up, using Cvent for invite sends, RSVP tracking, confirmations, reminders, and waitlist management.
  • Establish and maintain invitation lists in partnership with local offices and the email marketing team, and provide registration data and segments that support targeted sends.
  • Serve as the point of contact for registration questions, and resolve attendee issues quickly and courteously.
  • Administer post-event surveys in Cvent, monitor results, and share feedback with the event team to improve future events.

Virtual event portfolio

  • Own a portfolio of virtual events from planning through post-event follow-up, including timelines, run of show, speaker and presenter coordination, and attendee communications.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

Product Manager


About Computrition


Computrition, Inc. is a leading provider of enterprise foodservice, nutrition management, and retail technology, trusted by hundreds of organizations across North America, including healthcare systems, military installations, correctional facilities, and higher education institutions. For more than 44 years, we’ve built technology in partnership with our customers, helping them improve operational efficiency, strengthen financial performance, and deliver better nutritional care.


We’re investing in the future of our platform by adopting modern technologies and working closely with customers to solve complex operational challenges. Our solutions have real-world impact by driving performance enhancement and show up directly in how hospitals, military installations, and other institutions operate every day.


Computrition offers the stability of an established industry leader and the momentum of a company accelerating growth through innovation. We invest in our people and foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and professional growth where employees can make a meaningful impact. You’ll join experienced professionals who are passionate about solving meaningful problems and delivering measurable outcomes for customers.


With team members across the U.S. and Canada, and as part of a growing portfolio of technology companies owned by Constellation Software Inc. (TSX: CSU.TO), we are well-positioned to continue advancing the future of foodservice and nutrition technology.


If you’re looking to build technology that makes a meaningful impact while growing your career with a stable, innovative company, we’d like to hear from you.


About the Role


Computrition is seeking a Product Manager who combines product management expertise with strong commercial and strategic acumen. You will be primarily focused on Computrition’s next-generation, cloud-native food and nutrition management platform while also supporting our established customer base through ongoing enhancements and strategic product initiatives as business needs require.


As the Product Manager, you will report to the Director of Product and work closely with the EVP of Product. You will help shape product strategy and turn it into results. You take healthcare customer and prospect needs, competitive insight, and financial analysis and build them into differentiated products, strong business cases, and measurable growth.

You will work with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Design, and Engineering through the full product lifecycle: discovery, roadmap planning, delivery, launch, and adoption. You support ensuring product outcomes. That means supporting development of clear goals and success measures, making evidence-based prioritized trade-offs, and balancing customer value, usability, feasibility, and commercial return.

  • Directionally, you’ll split your time between:
    ~40% Discovery & Delivery: Customer conversations, requirements, backlog management, collaboration with Design & Engineering
  • ~30% Strategy & Business Cases: Market and competitive analysis, financial models, roadmap and executive materials
  • ~30% Commercialization: Positioning, pricing, packaging, launches & sales enablement

Of course, the time allocated to this and other responsibilities will be determined by business needs and priorities and may change from time to time.


Key Responsibilities


  • Strategy support: Partner with the Director of Product with product vision, strategy, and portfolio priorities. Prepare analysis, recommendations, and executive-ready materials for leadership reviews and investment decisions.
  • Market and customer insight: Talk with customers and prospects to confirm unmet needs, workflows, buying criteria, and willingness to pay. Analyze competitors and win/loss results to find where Computrition can stand apart and grow.
  • Roadmap and prioritization: Evaluate market opportunities and rank investments by validating demand, strategic fit, customer value, financial impact, and feasibility. Keep the roadmap current and clearly communicated.
  • Business cases: Build advanced Excel financial models covering revenue, pricing, costs, margin, ROI, and payback. Use scenario and sensitivity analysis to recommend investments and explain trade-offs.
  • Commercialization: Lead or contribute to positioning, pricing, packaging, and go-to-market plans. Support launches and give Sales clear value propositions, competitive guidance, demo narratives, and customer ROI tools.
  • Product delivery: Turn market needs into clear requirements, user stories, and prioritized backlog. Work with Design and Engineering in an Agile environment to deliver and validate customer value.
  • Performance Track adoption, retention, revenue, win rates, and profitability, and use the results to adjust strategy and the roadmap.
  • AI: Use AI responsibly to speed up research and product work. Evaluate AI-enabled product opportunities with attention to accuracy, privacy, and security.

Qualifications


Required

  • 4+ years in product management, management consulting, or strategy experience, with a record of SaaS product and commercial impact
  • Healthcare industry experience, including knowledge of clinical or operational workflows, purchasing processes, and privacy and regulatory requirements such as HIPAA
  • Strong strategic thinking and skill in market and competitive analysis
  • Advanced Excel and financial modeling, including business cases, forecasts, ROI analyses, and scenario models
  • Excellent written communication and executive presentation skills, plus the ability to influence across teams without direct authority
  • Familiarity with Pragmatic Institute (formerly Pragmatic Marketing) or similar frameworks, , and product planning tools such as Jira, Aha!, and ClickUp
  • Bachelor's degree in any field; Business, Economics, Finance, Marketing, and Healthcare Administration are all relevant

Preferred

  • Management consulting background (for example PwC, Deloitte, Accenture, or a comparable firm)
  • MBA or a related graduate degree
  • Experience with healthcare software, foodservice technology, clinical nutrition, or diet office operations
  • Experience moving customers from a legacy platform to SaaS or cloud
  • Experience working in an AI-driven development lifecycle, where requirements, specifications, and acceptance criteria are written so that both people and AI tools can act on them, and comfort adapting your practices as those methods evolve

What Success Looks like


First 90 Days

Develop a deep understanding of our customers, market dynamics, food and nutrition workflows, and platform capabilities. Build strong working relationships across Sales, Customer Success, Design, Engineering, Operations, and your Product Management colleagues. Conduct customer discovery interviews, market research, competitive analysis, and conversations with advisory board members to identify unmet needs, market trends, and growth opportunities. Become the owner of a defined product area, including its roadmap, backlog, key performance metrics, and strategic priorities. Begin evaluating potential product investments through preliminary business cases and commercial assessments.


First 6 Months

Deliver a prioritized product roadmap for your area, grounded in validated customer demand, market research, competitive insights, and business objectives. Develop and present at least one comprehensive business case, including market opportunity analysis, financial modeling, ROI projections, strategic rationale, and implementation recommendations. Partner with cross-functional teams to successfully launch a feature or product enhancement with clearly defined success metrics, adoption targets, and go-to-market support materials for Sales and Customer Success. Establish a regular cadence for gathering market intelligence and customer feedback to continuously inform product strategy and investment decisions.


Work Environment


This is a full-time remote position with about 25% travel for customer visits, team onsite meetings, conferences, and other work-related needs. We offer a flexible schedule, growth opportunities, comprehensive benefits, and pay based on experience.

Jonas Software is a leading provider of enterprise management software solutions, serving a wide range of vertical markets including hospitality, healthcare, construction, education, personal care, fitness, leisure, moving and legal services, to name a few. Within these markets, Jonas is comprised of over 65 distinct brands, each a respected leader in its domain.

Jonas’ vision is to be the branded global leader across these verticals and to be recognized by customers and industry stakeholders as the trusted provider of “Software for Life.” We are committed to technology, product innovation, quality, and exceptional customer service.

Jonas Software supports over 60,000 customers in more than 30 countries. We employ over 6,000 skilled professionals, including industry experts and technology specialists. Across our broader network, we support a global workforce of more than 30,000 employees.

Headquartered in Canada, Jonas Software has a global footprint with offices around the world. We’re a 100% owned subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc., based in Toronto, publicly listed on the TSX (CSU.TO), and a member of the S&P/TSX 60 Index.
