jobs.description:
Overview

Overview:

The Network Engineer is a core member of the Network Operations team responsible for designing, implementing, and optimizing HealthEdge’s enterprise network infrastructure across on-premises data centers, cloud environments, and remote access platforms. This role operates within a team-driven model emphasizing 24/7 availability, ITIL-aligned processes, automation, and measurable operational outcomes in support of our healthcare SaaS platform.

Essential Responsibilities:

Technical Execution & Operations

  • Design, configure, and maintain LAN/WAN, SD-WAN, VPN, firewall, and load-balancing infrastructure across multi-site and multi-cloud environments
  • Monitor network performance (SolarWinds, Datadog, ThousandEyes) and proactively resolve issues before they impact service delivery and SLA targets
  • Implement network security controls including firewall rule sets, IDS/IPS, segmentation, NAC, and zero-trust architecture principles
  • Design and manage AWS network infrastructure — VPCs, subnets, route tables, IGW, NAT Gateways, and ELBs — for scalable, highly available architectures
  • Configure AWS Transit Gateway and VPC peering for secure, low-latency connectivity across accounts, regions, and on-premises environments
  • Implement AWS Direct Connect and Site-to-Site VPN for hybrid connectivity between HealthEdge data centers and AWS
  • Administer AWS Route 53 including private hosted zones, resolver rules, and health-check-based routing policies
  • Manage AWS Security Groups, Network ACLs, AWS Network Firewall, and AWS Shield for least-privilege access and DDoS protection
  • Leverage AWS CloudWatch, VPC Flow Logs, and AWS Network Manager for observability, traffic analysis, and anomaly detection
  • Support Azure or GCP networking as required — VNets/VPCs, peering, and hybrid connectivity

Incident Response & Change Management

  • Participate in 24/7 on-call rotation, triaging and resolving network incidents per SLA targets; contribute to post-incident reviews to drive MTTR reduction
  • Execute network changes through established change management processes; serve as Tier 3 escalation resource for complex issues

Automation & Continuous Improvement

  • Develop automation scripts and IaC (Ansible, Terraform, CloudFormation, Python) to improve monitoring, alerting, and network deployment workflows
  • Build and maintain IaC for AWS network resources enabling repeatable, auditable deployments; surface optimization opportunities across the team’s roadmap

Documentation & Collaboration

  • Maintain topology diagrams, runbooks, IPAM, and change records; support DR testing, vendor coordination, and legacy environment consolidation
  • Collaborate across Infrastructure, Security, DevOps, and Application teams; mentor junior team members

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, IT, Network Engineering, or equivalent professional experience
  • 5+ years of hands-on enterprise network engineering or network operations experience
  • Strong knowledge of routing and switching protocols (BGP, OSPF, EIGRP, VLANs, STP)
  • Experience with enterprise firewall platforms (Palo Alto, Fortinet, Cisco ASA/FTD)
  • Demonstrated AWS networking expertise: VPC, Transit Gateway, Direct Connect, Route 53, Security Groups, Network ACLs, AWS Network Firewall
  • Proficiency with network monitoring tools (SolarWinds, Datadog, PRTG, or similar)
  • Experience with SD-WAN (Cisco Viptela, VMware VeloCloud, Fortinet, or equivalent)
  • Solid understanding of DNS, DHCP, IPAM, SSL/TLS, and PKI
  • Hands-on experience with IaC and automation tools (Ansible, Terraform, CloudFormation, Python)
  • Familiarity with ITIL-based incident, problem, and change management processes
  • Excellent analytical and communication skills; ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Certifications: CCNP, CCIE, PCNSE, NSE, or AWS Advanced Networking Specialty
  • Experience in healthcare SaaS or regulated environments (HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2)
  • Experience with large-scale infrastructure integrations or M&A network consolidation
  • Familiarity with HealthEdge products (HealthRules® Payer, HealthEdge Source™, GuidingCare®, Wellframe™)
  • Network automation experience at scale in a 24/7 operations environment

Geographic Responsibility: Remote, US

Type of Employment: Full-time, permanent

FLSA Classification (USA Only): Exempt

  • The employee is occasionally required to move around the office. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

jobs.title: Systems Engineer, Experiments & Integration (Mid/Senior/Principal)
jobs.excerpt: About Positron AI Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference.
jobs.description:
About Positron AI

Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference. Chips built for the training era keep running into two walls at inference time: memory bandwidth and chip-to-chip networking. We designed our architecture to break through both. Our first-generation Atlas systems are already in production on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Asimov, our first custom ASIC, takes that architecture to silicon. In simulations, Asimov delivers several times more tokens per dollar and tokens per watt than leading GPUs, at a fraction of the power. Paired in our Titan system, Asimov is built to serve models beyond 16 trillion parameters. In September 2026, we raised $875 million at a $5 billion valuation. NEA led the round, joined by Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, and others, to bring Asimov and Titan to market. Our team includes engineers from Groq, Lambda, NVIDIA, Meta, F5, and many other industry leaders.

Role Overview

As a Systems Engineer on our Experiments & Integration team, you will be the engineer who answers the urgent questions. Hardware, software, and customer teams bring the simulation team a steady stream of unplanned requests: run this model on the emulator, measure that bottleneck, help this team integrate. You will work across all of those teams, on both simulation and hardware emulation, to turn each request into a fast, measured answer.

The work is varied and hands-on: standing up a new model on the emulator, profiling where time goes, or trying a configuration a stakeholder wants to see. You will own this queue so the engineers building the roadmap can stay focused on it, and you will leave each investigation behind as a reusable model, test, or script.

Key Responsibilities

Rapid Response and Experiments

  • Serve as the first responder for simulation and emulation requests from hardware, software, and customer teams, partnering with the existing experiments and integration engineers so urgent asks get answered while roadmap work stays protected.
  • Run quick experiments and demos, such as getting a new LLM running on the emulator, profiling where time goes, or trying a configuration a stakeholder wants to see.

Performance Measurement

  • Measure and explain performance using counters, traces, and end-to-end timing, reported along with their limits and their drivers.

Integration and Reusable Assets

  • Help other teams build on the simulators and the emulation setup when they need integration support.
  • Convert each investigation into a reusable asset, such as a calibrated model, a repeatable experiment, or a regression test.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience as a hands-on systems or performance engineer.
  • Demonstrated experience running LLM inference workloads end to end and finding where time goes, including weight loading, memory bandwidth, and host-device synchronization.
  • A strong understanding of performance measurement, including counters, execution traces, profiling, and reporting results with their limits.
  • Hands-on experience with host-side driver and runtime code, and comfort working close to hardware.
  • Ability to move fast on loosely specified requests, make assumptions explicit, and finish by making the result repeatable.
  • Strong Rust skills, or expert-level C/C++ skills and a willingness to work in Rust day to day, along with proficiency in Python and fluency with Linux, shell scripting, containers, and CI.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to give stakeholders a direct answer, what it rests on, and what to do next.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with hardware emulators such as Cadence Palladium or Synopsys ZeBu, or with FPGA boards.
  • A track record of bringing up new workloads on early or unstable hardware.

Leveling & Scope

While this role is currently posted at a specific level, we are a growth-oriented organization and are open to hiring at a more senior level for the right candidate. Please note that this job description serves as a focused but generalized overview of the role; specific responsibilities and impact expectations will be tailored to the experience and seniority of the final hire.

Why Join Us?

  • You will see the whole stack, from emulated silicon to customer models, and be the person teams across the company rely on for fast, trustworthy answers.
  • Every investigation you run becomes lasting infrastructure that makes the next answer faster for everyone.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this role is Mid: $160,000-$220,000, Senior: $220,000–$270,000, Principal: $270,000-$350,000.

Please note that the figures provided represent the base salary range only and do not include other elements of our total compensation package, equity, or comprehensive benefits.

At Positron AI, we value the unique expertise each candidate brings. While the range above reflects our typical expectation for the position, we reserve the flexibility to exceed this range for candidates whose specialized skills, significant experience, or unique qualifications fall outside the standard scope of the role. Final offers are determined based on a variety of factors, including internal equity, and individual impact.

Benefits & Perks

We want you to do your best work and feel confident that you and your family are taken care of. That means comprehensive coverage, real time to rest, and support for your future.

Health and wellness

  • Fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your dependents
  • Company-paid life and disability coverage, with voluntary options to add more
  • Supplemental hospital, critical illness, and accident coverage available

Time off and flexibility

  • Unlimited paid time off; we encourage everyone to truly unplug and recharge
  • 13 paid company holidays
  • Remote-first culture with a company-provided computer and home office setup

Compensation and future

  • Competitive salary and equity
  • 401(k) with company matching, eligible from day one

Visa Support

This position is open to candidates currently authorized to work in the U.S. We cannot provide new visa sponsorship for this role but are open to facilitating H-1B visa transfers for eligible candidates.

Equal Opportunity Employer. If you're excited about the role but don't meet every bullet, we'd still love to hear from you.

About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Our teams work closely across product, engineering, customer success, sales, and company leadership to bring new capabilities to market and continuously improve the platform.

At Bask, reliable operations are an important part of delivering a consistent software experience. We value people who stay organized, take initiative, communicate clearly, and pay attention to the details that keep complex workflows moving. We believe strong operational coordination helps teams work more effectively and makes it easier to identify and resolve problems before they grow.

About the Role

We're looking for a Patient Care Operations Associate to support the administrative and operational processes connected to patient-facing workflows within Bask Health's telehealth platform.

This role focuses on non-clinical coordination, workflow monitoring, accurate documentation, and making sure operational issues reach the appropriate teams.

You'll help maintain organized processes that support patient-facing experiences without performing clinical work or making healthcare decisions.

Bask Health provides software that enables entrepreneurs, healthcare businesses, and online merchants to launch and manage direct-to-consumer telehealth services.

jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a Content Designer to help create clear, intuitive, and consistent content across Bask Health's software platform.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch and operate direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform connects merchant storefronts, patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

As a Content Designer, you'll help shape how people understand and interact with these experiences through thoughtful interface language, clear instructions, and well-structured information.

This is a hands-on product content role that combines UX writing, content design, information architecture, and collaboration with product and engineering teams. You'll work throughout the product development process, from understanding user needs and defining content requirements to writing, testing, and improving content in production.

Your work will span different areas of the platform, including merchant dashboards, patient onboarding, questionnaires, account settings, checkout, and operational workflows. You'll help ensure that users understand what actions they can take, what information they need to provide, and what happens next.

You'll write and improve interface copy such as navigation labels, buttons, form instructions, helper text, error messages, confirmation screens, empty states, and system notifications.

You'll also help organize information so complex product experiences are easier to navigate. This includes reviewing user journeys, identifying confusing terminology, and collaborating with designers to improve how content is presented within interfaces.

You'll work closely with product designers, product managers, engineers, researchers, and operational stakeholders to ensure content reflects actual product functionality and supports user needs.

As Bask continues expanding its platform, you'll contribute to reusable content patterns, terminology standards, and writing guidelines that help maintain consistency across different applications and merchant experiences.

Because Bask operates in healthcare-related environments, you'll need to approach sensitive information carefully. You'll collaborate with appropriate subject matter experts when content involves clinical, pharmacy, or regulated workflows, ensuring that language reflects approved processes and does not create misleading expectations.

You'll use usability research, product feedback, and available performance data to identify content problems and make improvements over time.

We're looking for someone who enjoys solving communication problems through product design, can simplify complicated information, and understands how thoughtful content helps people use software successfully.

What You'll Do

  • Create clear, concise, and user-friendly content across Bask Health's digital products.
  • Write interface copy for merchant-facing, patient-facing, and internal platform experiences.
  • Develop navigation labels, buttons, form instructions, helper text, and confirmation messages.
  • Improve error messages and recovery instructions so users understand how to resolve problems.
  • Design content for onboarding and account setup experiences.
  • Create clear instructions for multi-step workflows and configuration processes.
  • Collaborate with product designers to improve the usability of complex interfaces.
  • Work with product managers to understand product requirements and user needs.
  • Develop content for dashboards, settings pages, and administrative tools.
  • Improve content within questionnaires and form-based experiences.
  • Create clear empty states, loading messages, and system notifications.
  • Help users understand product features, available actions, and next steps.
  • Review existing interfaces to identify confusing or inconsistent terminology.
  • Develop reusable content patterns for common product interactions.
  • Contribute to Bask Health's content guidelines and design system.
  • Maintain consistent terminology across different areas of the platform.
  • Support information architecture improvements and content organization.
  • Collaborate with engineers to ensure content is implemented correctly.
  • Participate in product discovery and design discussions.
  • Review prototypes and provide content recommendations early in development.
  • Work with UX researchers to evaluate content comprehension and usability.
  • Use user feedback and research findings to improve interface language.
  • Apply accessibility and plain-language principles to product content.
  • Support content consistency across configurable merchant experiences.
  • Collaborate with clinical and pharmacy stakeholders when specialized terminology requires review.
  • Document content decisions, terminology guidelines, and reusable writing patterns.
  • Participate in design reviews and provide feedback on content quality.
  • Own assigned content design projects from initial requirements through implementation and iteration.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of professional experience in content design, UX writing, product content strategy, or a closely related field.
  • Portfolio or work samples demonstrating content design for digital products.
  • Strong writing, editing, and information organization skills.
  • Understanding of user-centered content design principles.
  • Experience writing interface content for web or mobile applications.
  • Ability to simplify complex information into clear, actionable language.
  • Experience creating labels, instructions, helper text, error messages, and confirmation copy.

Nice to Have

About SPUN

SPUN is an environmental nonprofit with a mission to map and protect the mycorrhizal networks that regulate Earth's climate and ecosystems. Since our founding in 2021, we have built a global data platform for these living underground networks, which move approximately 13 billion tons of CO2 into soils every year.

Through our Underground Explorers programme and a network of over 400 Science Associates across 80+ countries, we generate high-resolution datasets and mapping tools using machine learning, remote sensing and field-based sequencing. We turn that data into strategies for conservation, restoration, climate mitigation and sustainable land management.

We are a team of roughly 20 people at an inflection point: the science has matured, the policy landscape is moving, and the opportunity to embed mycorrhizal networks into global conservation, restoration, biodiversity and climate frameworks is real and time sensitive.

About the Role

The Project Manager is the operational partner to our Director of Global Policy & Impact. The Director is building the coalitions, policy relationships and cross-sector alliances that turn mycorrhizal data into above-ground decisions. You will make that work run: turning strategy into plans, keeping many parallel workstreams moving, and making sure SPUN shows up prepared, on time and credibly in the rooms where decisions are made.

Our theory of change runs from science and data, to translation for key decision-makers through coalitions and partnerships, driving tangible policy and practice adoption, which leads to improved decision-making outcomes and eventually long-term ecosystem impact and transformational shift in systems, mindsets and power. You will help ensure each link in that chain is planned, tracked and evidenced.

This is a hands-on role in a young, entrepreneurial organisation. You will manage projects, but also coordinate meetings and people across time zones, support funder reporting and help build the systems that let a startup NGO scale with integrity.

You will be the operational link across SPUN's policy and impact work, supporting two colleagues in particular. You will work with the International Policy Strategist / Advisor, who leads our engagement on the EU Soil Monitoring Law and the UNCCD, to keep their calendar, submissions and deliverables on track. And you will work with the Advocacy Lead, Mongolia, and the local team there (policy expert, Underground Explorers representative), whose workplan, risks and reporting feed into the portfolio you maintain.

What You'll Do

Strategy and planning

Support the Director in

  • Translating the global impact strategy and roadmap into workplans with clear objectives, priority geographies, owners, milestones and deadlines.
  • Maintaining an integrated view of all policy, coalition and advocacy workstreams, flagging risks, dependencies and decisions needed.
  • Helping keep policy and advocacy efforts aligned with SPUN's programmatic work by coordinating with the science, data, restoration, Underground Explorers and communications teams.
  • Maintain one integrated workplan and tracker covering the global, EU/UNCCD and Mongolia workstreams, and run a regular check-in rhythm across the Director, the International Policy Strategist / Advisor and the Advocacy Lead, Mongolia.

Stakeholder and coalition coordination

  • Maintain a stakeholder map and relationship tracker covering policymakers, NGOs and grassroots movements, practitioners, Indigenous and local communities, funders and scientists, with next steps and owners.
  • Plan and run logistics and follow-up for convenings and collaborative processes, including agendas, briefing packs, participant coordination and action tracking.
  • Support coalition and alliance activity across conservation, restoration, and biodiversity and climate networks, keeping commitments visible and moving.
  • Coordinate with partners and consultants in different regions and cultural contexts, with respect for community-driven and Indigenous-led approaches.

Policy and advocacy delivery

  • Maintain a calendar of multilateral, regional and standard-setting processes (for example the CBD, UNFCCC and EU legislation), with deadlines for submissions, side events and consultations.
  • Manage the production cycle for policy briefings, position papers and impact narratives, from drafting and scientific review to design and publication.
  • Help track impact of the Underground Explorers and Advocates network and turn data and stories the into materials for policymakers, practitioners and funders, working with the science and communications teams.
  • Support the Director for senior-level representation at international forums with briefings, speaking materials and follow-up actions.
  • Track how mycorrhizal science is being adopted into practitioner protocols, standards and decision-making tools.

Learning, impact and funding

  • Help define indicators and maintain a simple framework for tracking progress against the theory of change, from outputs through to policy and practice change.
  • Gather and synthesise insights from stakeholders, programme outcomes and SPUN's data to support learning and strategy adjustments.
  • Coordinate inputs for grant proposals and reports to funders, the board and public audiences, keeping deadlines and requirements on track.
  • Help maintain a pipeline of funding opportunities aligned with SPUN's science-to-policy and practice mission.
  • Track project budgets with our finance support and flag issues early.

Organisation and systems

  • Set up and improve lightweight project tools, templates and processes that fit a small team.
  • Keep documentation, trackers and shared files organised and easy to find.
  • Contribute to organisational culture, and support the executive team on projects when needed.

What We're Looking For

  • 4+ years of project or programme management experience, ideally in an environmental, conservation, policy, advocacy or international development setting.
  • Experience coordinating multi-stakeholder work across countries, such as coalitions, multi-partner projects or international convenings.
  • Comfort working with senior leaders, and the judgement to prepare briefings and anticipate what they will need.
  • Excellent organisation and the ability to manage many workstreams at once without losing detail.
  • Clear, concise writing, including editing and project-managing technical or policy documents.
  • Comfort with data and with turning programme information into credible reporting for funders and partners.
  • Experience in a small, entrepreneurial organisation where building systems from scratch is energising rather than uncomfortable.
  • Self-directed and autonomous, while collaborative and a strong team player.
  • Strong cultural competency and diplomatic skills, with respect for and awareness of Indigenous rights and community-driven conservation models.
  • Excellent oral and written English; other languages are a significant plus.
  • Confident with collaboration and project tools (such as Google Workspace and a task tool like Notion or Asana).

Nice to have

  • Familiarity with international biodiversity, climate or restoration policy processes.
  • Experience with grant management, funder reporting or monitoring, evaluation and learning.
  • Background in or genuine curiosity about ecology, soil science or fungi.
  • A project management qualification (PMP, PRINCE2, Agile), though practical experience matters more

What Makes This Role Distinctive

Mycorrhizal networks underpin nearly every terrestrial ecosystem on Earth, yet they remain almost entirely absent from the conservation, restoration and climate frameworks meant to protect them. SPUN has built the science to change that. As the person who keeps the policy and impact work organised and moving, you will be central to helping write a new chapter in how the world understands and acts on underground ecosystems.

What Success Looks Like

  • First 90 days: You understand SPUN's science, theory of change and priorities. You have mapped all live policy and impact workstreams, set up a simple planning and reporting rhythm the team uses, and built working relationships across the team and with key partners.
  • First 12 months: The Director has clear visibility of progress, risks and upcoming opportunities. Convenings, briefings and policy moments are delivered on time and to a high standard, and funders and the board receive timely, credible impact reporting.
  • Longer term: The coordination behind SPUN's policy and advocacy work is up to speed so that the Director can focus on relationships and influence, helping SPUN's data become indispensable to decision-makers and visible in changes in practice on the ground.

Why Join SPUN

At SPUN, we know that taking care of our team means empowering people to do their best work. Our benefits support health, well-being, growth, and balance. They are tailored to local laws so that everyone across our globally distributed team receives the same high standard of support.

We believe work should be both impactful and sustainable, and our benefits are designed to help you thrive in your role and beyond.

At SPUN, we embrace diversity as a fundamental pillar of our mission to protect underground ecosystems. Our commitment to decolonizing science depends on the diversity of knowledge and experience on our team and among our partners across the globe. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where all individuals, regardless of their race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or background, feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. We highly encourage individuals from traditionally underrepresented or marginalized groups, including but not limited to women, LGBTQIA+ people, individuals from the Global South, and individuals with Indigenous heritage, to apply to join our team at SPUN.

To learn more about our organization and culture, please visit our website .

jobs.excerpt: About CollectlyCollectly is a fast-growing healthcare technology company transforming revenue cycle management (RCM) through AI-driven automation.
jobs.description:
About Collectly

Collectly is a fast-growing healthcare technology company transforming revenue cycle management (RCM) through AI-driven automation. Millions of patients navigate inefficient billing systems every day, while providers face delayed payments, rising administrative burden, and operational complexity.

Collectly applies artificial intelligence to automate workflows, accelerate cash flow, and modernize the patient financial experience; enabling healthcare organizations to operate more efficiently and focus on delivering care.

There could not be a hotter space to play in. Healthcare is a $4.9T industry and is adopting AI technology at 2.2x the rate of the rest of the economy. RCM is at the heart of this transformation as it has a clear and demonstrable ROI to our customers.

The Opportunity

    Every patient who receives a medical bill has questions: what is this charge, will my insurance cover it, can I pay it in parts, why is it different from last time. How those questions get answered decides whether the patient pays, calls back, or gives up.

    Collectly's AI agent, Billie, answers those questions today across chat, SMS, and voice for hundreds of medical practices nationwide. We are looking for a Product Manager to own the patient experience around it: what Billie handles, how she interacts with clinic staff, how we reach patients proactively, and how we prove to our customers that it works.

    This is a hands-on product ownership role at a small, fast-moving product team. Some of the work is taking a product area from 1 to 10, where the problem is still being discovered with customers. Some of it is taking an area from 10 to 100, where something that works for one customer has to work for every customer without being rebuilt each time. You will work directly with founders, customers, engineering, data, and the implementation teams, and you will see what you decide in production within weeks.

Key Responsibilities

    - Lead product discovery with customers — billing leaders, support managers, front-desk staff — and turn what you learn into a prioritized roadmap for patient experience.

    - Own the patient experience end to end: define the set of patient situations that decide whether the experience is good — the questions patients ask, the hand-offs to staff, the dead ends — and work with engineering to make the product handle each one well.

    - Design proactive patient outreach — who is contacted, on which channel, when, with what message — and measure the effect on patient satisfaction and on revenue collected.

    - Define and own the metrics for the patient-facing product — escalation rate, self-service rate, patient satisfaction, payment outcomes — and use them to decide what gets built next.

    - Analyze product performance directly: query the data warehouse, read real patient conversations, find where the agent falls short and why.

    - Prototype with AI tools before specifying: build the mock, the script, or the analysis that settles the question.

    - Partner with engineering on agent behavior, prompts, EHR and practice-management integrations, and where human-in-the-loop belongs.

    - Scale what works across the customer base: turn one-off configurations into features every practice gets, instead of rebuilding per customer.

    - Lead technical customer projects: launch new customers and new capabilities with implementation and customer success, and own the first weeks after go-live.

    - Keep the customer-facing material current for pre-service and patient support: case studies with real numbers, working demos, and sales playbooks.

What Success Looks Like

    Within the first 6 months, you will:

    - Define a set of cases that determine a great patient experience and work with engineering teams to optimize the product to fit those cases
    - Design proactive patient outreach flows and evaluate how they impact patient satisfaction and patient revenue
    - Decide how to increase resolution rates for Collectly patient support and which products to build to resolve those requests
    - Update case studies, demos and sales playbooks for Collectly pre-service and patient support products

Qualifications

    Required

    - Experience in US healthcare (must-have!): RCM, eligibility, claims, payments, payer-provider workflows
    - 3+ years of product management experience in technical B2B products, with full ownership of what gets built and why

    - A track record of quantified business outcomes: revenue, cost reduction, conversion, automation rate, or efficiency

    - Direct customer-facing experience with B2B customers; enterprise experience preferred

    - Experience launching new products, not only features within existing ones

    - Hands-on with AI tools: able to build prototypes and run analyses with Claude or similar

    - Strong analytical skills; comfortable writing code and SQL with AI while doing your own analysis

    - Ability to fly to San Francisco for an onsite interview with the team (at our costs)

    Core Competencies

    - Customer discovery

    - Product ownership and decision-making

    - Data-driven decision making

    - Analytical depth and curiosity
    - Leading technical customer projects

    - Hands-on mindset

    Preferred

    - A previous role in engineering, data science, or analytics
    - Startup or small-product-team background; founder or early-stage experience

    - Experience working on AI/ML products

Why You’ll Love It Here

  • Unlimited PTO: We believe in work-life balance and encourage you to recharge when you need it.

  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Fully paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your dependents, because your well-being matters to us.

  • Equity Opportunities: Share in our success with stock options - your hard work will drive our growth.

  • Retirement Planning Made Easy: Enjoy a 401(k) with a generous company match to secure your future.

  • Student Loan Support: We help lighten the load with contributions toward your student loans.

  • Compensation Range: 160-210k/year

Collectly is a tech-enabled patient billing platform that works as an add-on for your EHR/PM. Collectly accelerates and increases patient cash flow, streamlines post-service billing operations, and provides the best patient experience that works for all demographics.
Please, see a short video about us

Together, we have the opportunity – and the power – to continue to revolutionize the technology behind air conditioning, heating and refrigeration, and cultivate a better future. Learn more about us and how you can join our team!

Overview

We are looking for a DevOps Engineer with a strong Java background to build, automate, and operate the infrastructure that powers our healthcare technology platform. You will be the connective tissue between development and operations — accelerating delivery pipelines, strengthening cloud infrastructure, and ensuring the reliability of critical healthcare systems.

As a DevOps Engineer, this is your opportunity to:

  • Design, implement, and maintain CI/CD pipelines for Java-based microservices and enterprise healthcare applications using tools like GitLab CI/CD, Jenkins, or similar.

  • Handle storage and access configurations such as S3 bucket policies, IAM roles, file permissions, and mount/server path configurations (EFS/NFS).

  • Write and maintain automation scripts using Bash, Shell, or Python for deployment and operational tasks.
  • Manage source control and branching strategies using Git (GitLab), including integration with CI/CD pipelines.
  • Apply security best practices in CI/CD, infrastructure, and application deployment (secrets management, IAM policies, vulnerability scanning).
  • Support containerization and orchestration using Docker and Kubernetes (EKS or on-prem clusters).
  • Collaborate with Java development teams to embed DevOps practices throughout the software delivery lifecycle
  • Ensure system reliability, performance, and security compliance across healthcare environments
  • Support integration with healthcare ecosystem partners

jobs.description:
Job Description: English Language Expert – Australia & New Zealand

Role Type: Contractor
Location: Remote (Australia or New Zealand)

About the Role

We are seeking English Language Experts from Australia and New Zealand to support an AI training project focused on improving speech recognition and language understanding. You will use your knowledge of regional accents, dialects, vocabulary, and language variations to review audio recordings and improve transcription accuracy.

Key Responsibilities

  • Listen to multi-speaker audio recordings and identify speaker and audio metadata, including dialect, accent, audio quality, background noise, age, and speaking style.
  • Review and correct first-pass ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) transcripts using Australian and New Zealand English conventions.
  • Identify and categorize regional accents, including General, Broad, and Cultivated Australian English, Aboriginal English, Māori English, and Pasifika-influenced English.
  • Recognize community and regional language variations, including those influenced by Italian, Greek, Vietnamese, and Lebanese heritage communities.
  • Distinguish Australian and New Zealand speakers using pronunciation and linguistic features, including the New Zealand short-front vowel shift.
  • Apply knowledge of local vocabulary, idioms, slang, Māori expressions, code-switching, and spelling conventions.
  • Ensure accurate and consistent language annotation according to project guidelines.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Fluent proficiency in Australian and/or New Zealand English, with familiarity across regional accents and dialects.
  • Background in linguistics, language teaching, transcription, editing, translation, journalism, or a related field.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to distinguish subtle differences in Australian and New Zealand pronunciation, vocabulary, and usage.
  • Experience with audio annotation, metadata tagging, or transcription is an advantage.
  • Ability to work independently and follow detailed annotation guidelines.
  • Interest in linguistic technology, AI training, or language data projects is a plus.

jobs.description:
Position Overview

August Synergy Group (ASG), an 8(a)-eligible joint venture affiliated with CETECHS, is seeking experienced Mortality Coders, ICD-10 Cause-of-Death Coding Specialists, and Nosologists to support an anticipated federal contract with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS).

We are particularly interested in individuals with previous or current experience supporting CDC mortality coding programs, including incumbent personnel interested in continuing their work under a new contractor.

This position involves reviewing, interpreting, and assigning ICD-10 codes to causes of death reported on death certificates and fetal death records. Successful candidates will support the accuracy, consistency, and quality of national mortality statistics.

This position requires specialized mortality coding experience. Traditional ICD-10-CM medical billing and reimbursement coding experience alone may not meet the qualifications.

Key Responsibilities

  • Review and assign ICD-10 cause-of-death codes to mortality and fetal death records.

  • Perform manual coding of records that cannot be processed through automated coding systems.

  • Apply applicable ICD-10 mortality coding conventions, rules, and procedures.

  • Review and resolve complex or ambiguous cause-of-death statements.

  • Support quality assurance, quality control, and coding accuracy initiatives.

  • Identify and correct coding discrepancies.

  • Participate in recoding and validation activities as assigned.

  • Maintain coding accuracy consistent with CDC performance standards.

  • Meet established productivity, turnaround, and quality requirements.

  • Participate in required training and maintain proficiency with updated coding guidance.

  • Protect confidential government information and comply with applicable security requirements.

  • Collaborate with project leadership and other coding specialists to meet contract deliverables.

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience with ICD-10 mortality cause-of-death coding, preferably supporting CDC, NCHS, state vital records programs, or similar public health mortality coding operations.

  • Knowledge of mortality coding rules, conventions, and procedures.

  • Ability to interpret medical terminology and causes of death documented on death certificates.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to consistently produce accurate coding results.

  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.

  • Strong organizational, communication, and time-management skills.

  • Ability to complete required federal background screening and obtain necessary government system access.

Contracts Administrator (Legal Operations, CLM & Contract Lifecycle Management) – Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Contracts Administrator to manage the complete contract lifecycle—from intake and drafting through execution, renewals, compliance tracking, and reporting.

This is a highly detail-oriented, process-driven role responsible for ensuring contracts move efficiently, accurately, and compliantly across Legal, Sales, Procurement, Finance, Security, and Executive teams. You’ll oversee contract workflows, coordinate approvals, maintain CLM systems, track renewals, and support audit readiness while helping build scalable legal operations.

If you thrive in structured, high-volume environments and enjoy creating organized, efficient systems, this role offers excellent ownership and long-term growth.

Responsibilities

Contract Lifecycle Management

  • Manage contracts from intake through drafting, review, approval, execution, storage, renewals, and reporting.
  • Ensure agreements are accurate, compliant, fully executed, searchable, and audit-ready.
  • Maintain contract repositories and ensure complete documentation throughout the contract lifecycle.

Contract Drafting, Review & Redlining

  • Draft, review, and manage agreements including:
    • NDAs
    • DPAs
    • Statements of Work (SOWs)
    • Master Service Agreements (MSAs)
    • Vendor Agreements
    • Order Forms
    • Partner and Reseller Agreements
  • Redline contracts using Microsoft Word Track Changes.
  • Escalate non-standard legal terms involving indemnification, limitation of liability, intellectual property, data privacy, termination clauses, and service level agreements.
  • Maintain deviation logs, approval records, and contract history.

Approvals & Governance

  • Coordinate contract approvals across Legal, Finance, Procurement, Security, Information Security, Sales, and Executive teams.
  • Verify commercial terms align with pricing and business requirements.
  • Ensure vendor onboarding documentation is complete, including:
    • W-9 forms
    • Certificates of Insurance (COIs)
    • Banking information
    • Compliance documentation

Contract Execution & Repository Management

  • Manage electronic signature workflows using DocuSign or Adobe Sign.
  • Verify signer authority, signature blocks, and execution completeness.
  • Maintain agreements within CLM platforms such as Ironclad, Icertis, Agiloft, ContractWorks, Conga, SharePoint, or similar systems.
  • Ensure metadata remains accurate, including contract value, effective dates, renewal terms, jurisdiction, and privacy addenda.

Renewals, Compliance & Risk Management

  • Track contract renewals, notice periods, pricing changes, deliverables, and contractual obligations.
  • Send proactive renewal reminders to internal stakeholders.
  • Support compliance with GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOX, and other applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Maintain organized, audit-ready documentation and approval records.

Reporting & Process Improvement

  • Prepare reports covering:
    • Contract cycle times
    • SLA performance
    • Renewal pipeline
    • Contract deviations
    • Standard versus non-standard agreements
  • Improve contract templates, clause libraries, approval workflows, and CLM processes.
  • Help scale legal operations through workflow automation and documentation improvements.

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • Highly organized with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Process-driven and comfortable managing high-volume contract workflows.
  • Strong communicator who collaborates effectively across multiple departments.
  • Able to identify contractual risks, inconsistencies, and missing information quickly.
  • Passionate about building efficient, scalable operational systems.

Required Experience & Skills

  • 2+ years of experience in Contracts Administration, Legal Operations, or Contract Coordination.
  • Hands-on experience with CLM platforms such as Ironclad, Icertis, Agiloft, ContractWorks, Conga, SharePoint, or similar systems.
  • Strong proficiency with:
    • Microsoft Word Track Changes
    • Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets
    • PDF editing software
  • Working knowledge of:
    • NDAs
    • DPAs
    • MSAs
    • Confidentiality agreements
    • Indemnification
    • Intellectual property clauses
    • Limitation of liability
    • Service Level Agreements (SLAs)
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.

Nice to Have

  • Experience supporting GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOX, or other regulated environments.
  • Experience with both buy-side and sell-side contracts.
  • Exposure to procurement, vendor onboarding, vendor risk management, or security questionnaires.
  • Experience developing clause libraries, contract templates, and legal playbooks.

What Success Looks Like

  • Contract cycle times consistently meet SLA targets.
  • Zero missed renewals, notice periods, or contractual obligations.
  • Accurate and complete contract repository with 100% metadata accuracy.
  • High percentage of agreements executed using approved standard language.
  • Audit-ready documentation maintained at all times.
  • Continuous improvements in legal operations through process optimization.

Interview Process

  • Initial Phone Screen
  • Video Interview with Pavago Recruiter
  • Practical Assessment (NDA Redlining & Contract Tracking Exercise)
  • Client Interview
  • Offer & Background Verification

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. This short, self-recorded video is the final step that completes your application.

Instead of repeating yourself across multiple screening calls, you’ll introduce yourself once, and your video will be shared with the hiring team. This allows hiring managers to assess your communication style early, making future interviews more meaningful while reducing unnecessary interview rounds.

Don’t overthink it—you can record your video as many times as you’d like before submitting it. Only your final submission will be reviewed. Please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for your Spark Hire invitation.

About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a Product Design Intern to join Bask Health and gain hands-on experience designing intuitive, functional, and visually polished software experiences.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform connects merchant tools, patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce capabilities.

As a Product Design Intern, you'll work alongside experienced designers, product managers, and engineers to help improve how people interact with our products.

This internship is designed for students, recent graduates, and aspiring product designers who want to develop practical UX and UI design skills while contributing to real product initiatives.

You'll have opportunities to support interface design, wireframing, prototyping, user flows, and design system improvements.

Your projects may involve merchant dashboards, onboarding experiences, patient questionnaires, account settings, administrative interfaces, or other areas of the platform.

You'll learn how product teams identify user problems, evaluate possible solutions, and translate requirements into functional interface designs.

You'll use Figma to create wireframes, interface mockups, interactive prototypes, and design documentation.

You'll also learn how design decisions connect to business requirements, user needs, and technical constraints.

You'll participate in design reviews and collaborate with product managers to understand feature requirements and priorities.

You'll also have opportunities to work with engineers and learn how design specifications are translated into working software.

You'll become familiar with Bask Health's design system and help maintain consistency across product experiences.

You'll learn how usability research, user feedback, and product observations can inform design decisions.

Because Bask operates in healthcare-related environments, you'll also learn the importance of clarity, accessibility, privacy, and accuracy when designing patient-facing and operational experiences.

You'll receive guidance on assigned projects and have opportunities to take increasing ownership of clearly defined design tasks as your skills develop.

We're looking for someone who is curious, creative, detail-oriented, open to feedback, and excited to build practical product design experience.

  • Collaborate with engineers to understand implementation requirements.
  • Help prepare design files and specifications for development handoff.
  • Support design quality assurance by reviewing implemented interfaces.
  • Identify visual inconsistencies and opportunities for improvement.
  • Maintain organized Figma files and project documentation.
  • Learn how product design fits into the software development process.
  • Complete assigned design tasks with guidance and regular feedback.

Requirements

Help Modernize the U.S. Army's Global Network!

Leidos has an immediate opening for a Mid-Level Network Integration Engineer to support the Army Global Unified Network (AGUN) program.

This is an exciting opportunity to help modernize, integrate, and secure the Army's global enterprise network, supporting critical military communications worldwide.

In this remote role, you'll work with experienced network engineers and technical teams to support network integration, routing and switching, SD-WAN connectivity, troubleshooting, and infrastructure modernization.

We're looking for someone with strong hands-on networking experience who enjoys solving technical challenges, integrating complex network systems, and supporting mission-critical infrastructure.


What You'll Do

  • Support the engineering and integration of network services across the Army's global network.
  • Perform network device discovery, validate management connectivity, and identify migration dependencies.
  • Assist with network migration planning, implementation, testing, troubleshooting, and post-migration validation.
  • Support SD-WAN, MPLS, VPN, and enterprise LAN/WAN connectivity.
  • Configure and troubleshoot VRFs, routing tables, and network segmentation.
  • Perform network device upgrades, patching, configuration changes, and lifecycle maintenance.
  • Troubleshoot network connectivity, performance, and security issues.
  • Work with engineering teams to assess legacy network environments and support modernization efforts.
  • Support DoD security requirements, including STIG implementation and network hardening.
  • Coordinate with stakeholders during network integration, testing, and migration activities.
  • Develop and maintain site integration plans, network diagrams, configuration documentation, test configurations, and migration validation records.
  • Collaborate with senior engineers and cybersecurity teams to resolve complex technical issues.
  • Work independently on assigned engineering tasks while escalating advanced issues when needed.

What We're Looking For

  • Active DoD Secret security clearance and U.S. citizenship.
  • Bachelor's degree in a related technical field with 4–8 years of relevant experience, or approximately 8–12 years of relevant experience without a degree.
  • DoD 8570/8140 IAT Level II certification (such as Security+) and an approved Computing Environment (CE) certification.
  • Strong hands-on experience with enterprise routing, switching, network integration, and troubleshooting.
  • Knowledge of LAN/WAN, BGP, TCP/UDP, IPSec, VPNs, Layer 2/Layer 3 routing, MPLS, and firewalls.
  • Experience with network device patching, upgrades, configuration management, and lifecycle maintenance.
  • Experience with at least one network management platform, such as:
    • Palo Alto Panorama
    • Cisco Prime
    • Cisco DNA
    • Junos Space
  • Hands-on experience with at least two of the following:
    • Cisco
    • Juniper
    • Palo Alto
    • Dell Networking
    • Remote Access VPN (RAVPN)
    • GlobalProtect
    • AppGate
  • Experience implementing DoD STIGs and network security hardening.
  • Familiarity with SFTP, SSH, SCP, SNMP, and NTP.
  • Strong troubleshooting, communication, and customer-facing skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaborate with geographically dispersed teams.
  • Flexibility to work nonstandard shifts to support network integration and migration activities.
  • Willingness to travel up to 10%.

jobs.description:
About Redesign Group

The Redesign Group is a global technology and cybersecurity Solution Provider leveraging design thinking, interdependent subject matter expertise, and emerging technology solutions to help organizations achieve meaningful transformation. Our globally diverse team members, partnerships with strategic technology manufacturers, and cybersecurity services position us to be a business partner that’s ready for what’s next.

We live by our core values of operating in the service of others, being problem solvers, and focusing on long term partnerships. You’ll excel at Redesign if you thrive in a rewarding environment that moves quickly, challenges you to grow and fosters collaboration. We seek candidates with a hands-on customer-first approach, robust interpersonal and communication skills, strong work ethic and excellent time management. While teamwork is expected, the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment is crucial.

Job Description

The Associate Cloud Engineer keeps our clients' cloud environments healthy day to day. You will work inside the baselines and runbooks our senior engineers have set: working monitoring alerts and tickets, applying patches and updates, executing documented changes, and learning the platforms from the engineers who own them. You will work from a ticketing system against defined service level objectives, supported by a global network operations center that handles first-line monitoring and intake.

Our clients run primarily on Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365, with AWS and Google Cloud in a growing minority of environments and Redesign Cloud for hosted workloads. We do not expect you to have run production cloud environments yet, but we do expect foundational knowledge of one major cloud provider, basic scripting ability, and the appetite to build depth in the rest.

Key Responsibilities

  • Work cloud and infrastructure alerts and tickets in priority order, resolving what is in scope and escalating with clear detail when it is not.
  • Perform routine operational tasks across Azure, Microsoft 365, and AWS, including patching, backup verification, access requests, and resource tagging.
  • Execute documented changes such as VM resizing, storage expansion, network security group updates, and policy adjustments through structured change management.
  • Monitor platform health, capacity, and cost dashboards and flag risks to senior engineers before they become incidents.
  • Review cloud cost and usage reports and raise rightsizing and cleanup opportunities for senior engineers to approve.
  • Assist senior engineers on cloud projects, migrations, and remediation work, taking ownership of defined tasks.
  • Support incident response by gathering evidence, building timelines, and contributing to root cause analyses.
  • Maintain and improve runbooks, knowledge base articles, and environment documentation as you learn.
  • Script small repeatable tasks in PowerShell, Azure CLI, or Python with guidance from senior engineers.
  • Give client contacts and internal teams clear status reporting on the tickets and changes you own.

Required Skills & Experience

  • Foundational knowledge of Microsoft Azure or AWS covering compute, storage, networking, and identity concepts.
  • Working knowledge of Windows Server and Linux basics, Active Directory and Entra ID, and Microsoft 365 administration.
  • Aptitude for automation using AI tooling and basic scripting (PowerShell, Bash, or Python), and the willingness to build that skill further.
  • Comfort working from a ticketing system and following documented procedures and change management precisely.
  • Strong troubleshooting instincts and the discipline to document what you did and why.
  • Clear written and verbal communication with clients and internal teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Microsoft AZ-900 or AZ-104, AWS Cloud Practitioner or Solutions Architect Associate, or comparable cloud certifications.
  • Exposure to infrastructure as code such as Bicep or Terraform, or to monitoring tooling such as Azure Monitor or CloudWatch.
  • Internship, lab, or home-lab experience building and breaking cloud environments.

Background

  • 0 to 2 years in IT support, systems administration, or cloud operations, or a recent graduate with hands-on lab experience.
  • Exposure to supporting more than one environment at a time, ideally in a managed services or help desk setting.
  • Associate's or bachelor's degree in information technology or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience.

Benefits

We offer a comprehensive benefits package which may include:

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match (annual dollar cap applied)
  • Flexible time off plan
  • 15 paid holidays
  • Sick leave (amount varies by state requirements and is at least the minimum required by any state)
  • Short-term and long-term disability
  • Life insurance
  • Paid parental leave

We’re an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. We consider qualified candidates without regard to any legally protected status. This role is subject to applicable employment laws based on work location. In compliance with pay transparency laws, the compensation range for this role is included, with final pay based on experience, skills, and location. jobs.excerpt: About GiveDirectlyWhat if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

jobs.description:
About GiveDirectly

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

  1. Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.
  2. Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.
  3. Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.
  4. Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.
  5. Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.
  6. Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.
  7. Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.
  8. Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.

If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.

Want to learn more? Read and listen:

We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

About this role

The Finance team supports all financial activities in 10 countries, 9 of them in Africa. As part of the global finance team, you will run payment cycles across multiple countries and make them faster and more accurate. You’ll also support country finance operations, working closely with the rest of the Finance team.

You are a great candidate for this role if you have hands-on payments experience, strong numerical skills, learn new systems quickly, and already use technology and AI tools to work smarter.

Reports to: Finance Manager

Level: Officer

Location:This role is open only to candidates based in Rwanda, DRC, Malawi, Kenya or Uganda, where we can employ you directly through a GiveDirectly entity.

Travel Requirement: Must be able to travel 1-2 times per year to one of our countries of operation for team retreats or colocations

What you’ll do:

  • Payments and treasury
    • Run payment cycles in multiple countries end to end: preparing, validating and issuing payments, and resolving exceptions and failed payments quickly.
    • Reconcile payments with bank and mobile money statements, and investigate and clear any differences.
    • Support account funding, cash forecasting, and FX across multiple currencies to ensure payments are never delayed.
    • Work with banks, mobile money operators and country teams to fix payment and funding issues.
    • Improve and standardise payment processes across countries, and document them in clear SOPs.
    • Use automation and AI tools to improve payment accuracy, speed and reporting.
  • Country finance operations
    • Support country finance operations, e.g., petty cash counts, asset counts, and finance liaison with authorities on tax and statutory filings.
    • Support the wider Finance team as needed to meet department goals.
  • Risk and compliance
    • Apply strong controls in every payment process, including maker-checker, audit trails and segregation of duties.
    • Handle recipient and payment data securely, and flag fraud risks early.
    • Understand and implement compliance requirements from tax regulators and payment partners.
    • Support in-country audits and special reporting to donors and regulators on request.

What you’ll bring:

  • Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. We welcome and strongly encourage applications from candidates who have personal or professional experience in the low-income and/or historically marginalized communities that we serve.
  • A bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting or a related field, or equivalent experience. A professional qualification (ACCA, CIMA, CPA or similar, completed or in progress) is a plus.
  • 2+ years of professional experience in accounting or finance, including at least 1 year running payments. For example: bulk or high-volume disbursements, bank and mobile money transfers, payment reconciliations and fixing failed payments.
  • Strong numerical skills and close attention to detail. You can reconcile large datasets accurately under deadline pressure and catch errors before they reach recipients.
  • Advanced Excel or Google Sheets (e.g. XLOOKUP, SUMIFS, pivot tables, data validation), and experience with finance and payments software (e.g. Intacct, Tipalti, Emburse, QuickBooks, online banking platforms).
  • You use AI tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT) every day to work faster and better, for example to analyse data, draft procedures or investigate exceptions. You check AI output carefully and handle sensitive data responsibly.
  • You learn quickly and do well in a fast-paced, high-volume environment where priorities and processes change often.
  • Fluent English. Working knowledge of French or Portuguese is an advantage.

Compensation

At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third-party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no-negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here.

The compensation for this role across the various locations is as shown below:

Kenya:

Base Salary: $16,030

Bonus at Target Performance: 10%

Rwanda:

Base Salary: $13,810

Bonus at Target Performance: 10%

Uganda:

Base Salary: $14,840

Bonus at Target Performance: 10%

Why work at GiveDirectly?

At GiveDirectly, we work to ensure that you have everything you need to excel in your role and on your team, including:

  • A supportive team that works hard and cares hard
  • A robust health benefits plan (exact details will vary by country)
  • Flexible paid time off that staff is encouraged to take
  • Allowances for desk set-up and learning and development

Working at GiveDirectly

GiveDirectly is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to the person’s race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Flagging for US applicants: We invite you to "Know Your Rights" as an applicant.

Commitment to Safeguarding

As a global organization working with communities to eliminate extreme poverty, GiveDirectly takes the safeguarding of its recipients, staff, and partners seriously. To that end, GiveDirectly is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and will systematically check with previous employers about any abuse or misconduct related matters involving potential new hires. We may also employ other robust pre-hire screens, including in-depth reference checks, criminal background checks, and sanctions screens.

These efforts help us continue to build and maintain trust with the communities we work with, and prevent abuse to our recipients and staff.

**GD is committed to observing all local, national and international laws that protect people and basic human rights of all. GD is committed to a policy of “zero tolerance when it comes to preventing, reporting, or responding to any form of abuse or exploitation.” and expects anyone who works for GD to uphold the protection and safeguarding of our recipients as a priority.**

About Us

Trase is the operating system for high-stakes environments, providing end-to-end solutions for deploying, managing, and optimizing AI within industries where security, governance, and data sovereignty are non-negotiable.

Our HIPAA- and SOC 2-compliant platform bridges the “last mile” of AI adoption, empowering sectors like healthcare and national security to run trustworthy, predictable AI agents across any model or environment—whether in the cloud, on-prem, or at the edge—with unified policy enforcement, continuous monitoring, and fully immutable audit trails.

Trase’s suite of products includes Origin, its agentic operating system; Leagues, its marketplace for specialized, configurable, ready-to-deploy agents; and Arena, where developers build, evaluate, and package the agents that run on Origin. Trase is AI, Uncomplicated. Co-founded in 2023 by Joe Laws and Grant Verstandig, Trase is an end-to-end platform for deploying, managing, and optimizing AI in the enterprise—bridging the “last mile” of AI adoption to drive efficiency and significant cost savings.

jobs.title: PPC Marketing Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Everyone can run a search campaign.  Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.
